# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume, and a repo-wide guard asserts it.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the shared rule and the guard; `npm test` for the new files passes.
- The unit tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`) and cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — new.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend guard.
- `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — shared guard helper (extend if needed).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.

# Test: gyms drop minerals on kill

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic gym tests that fail while the gyms do not drop minerals, pinning the behaviour the gym-wiring task must deliver.

## Required coverage

- Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row (via the shared destruction path and via the EXPLODE button) increases the live mineral count by exactly one at the asteroid's position.
- A large/medium asteroid splits into its children without a direct mineral drop.
- No double drop: a single destruction produces exactly one drop (not one per path).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the gym drop behaviour; `npm test` for the gym suites passes.
- Tests assert the drop position and count, not merely that the count increased, and are deterministic (seeded RNG).
- Tests fail before the gym-wiring task lands and pass after it.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`

# Shared player-control step across all scenes

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 1 & 11).

## Summary

The sequence *input → tick weapon timers → apply P5 speed/fire-rate multipliers → physics → auto-fire* is re-implemented in `PlayScene.tick`, `GymFormationScene.tick`, `GymWeapons.tick`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` and `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick`, and `GymPlayer.update` inlines the scheme→input mapping instead of the shared `_readPlayerInput`. Extract one `_tickPlayer(dt)` (and keep `_readPlayerInput`) in `CombatCoreScene` so every scene advances the player identically.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — `CombatCoreScene` owns a single `_tickPlayer(dt)` that performs, in the same order every frame: `tickWeaponTimers`, live `setSpeedMultiplier`/`setFireRateMultiplier` from the effects registry, `_readPlayerInput`→`setInput`, `physicsTick`, and `_autoFire`. `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene`, `GymWeapons` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` call it instead of their local copy. Verified by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **AC2** — `GymPlayer` consumes the shared input mapping (calls `_readPlayerInput` or an extracted shared input helper) and no longer inlines the `fourDirHandler`/`asteroidsHandler` branch. Verified by a source guard and by `GymPlayer.test.ts`.
- [ ] **AC3** — Timed-weapon expiry, P5 multipliers and auto-fire ordering are identical in the game and every gym for the same input and `dt`. Verified by a cross-scene equivalence test booting `PlayScene` and a gym, applying a P5 effect and asserting the same speed/fire-rate outcome.
- [ ] **AC4** — `GymPowerUpsCombat` no longer uses a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the player path; the player is advanced from the supplied `dt` (the enemy-clock fix is child #2).
- [ ] **AC5** — All existing scene suites pass unchanged; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard covers `_tickPlayer`.
- [ ] **AC6** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md` and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4.
- [ ] **AC7** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC7)** — [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — new shared `_tickPlayer(dt)`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — consume the shared step.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — coverage.

## Open questions

- **OQ8 (from epic):** should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal? *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper.*

## Plan — changelog

- 2026-09-26 — `/skill:plan AH-0MUII39KX007YUQ0`: autoplan pre-check returned `decision: skip` (placeholder effort Extra Small / risk Low). Planning auto-completed via the six automated review stages. No child items were created: the parent epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` already decomposed register gaps 1 & 11 into this leaf task, and its ACs contain the test/verification obligations. No blocking clarifications were required; clarifications and one flagged AC wording issue are recorded below.

## Plan — automated review summary

Retained as a leaf task for direct implementation (measurable ACs + minimal implementation sketch):

- **Requirements & AC alignment:** AC1–AC7 trace to epic gaps 1 (player-control step duplicated) and 11 (`GymPlayer` not on the shared control core). AC1 names four consumers; AC2 covers `GymPlayer`; AC4 covers `GymPowerUpsCombat`; together they cover every consumer named in the summary. OQ8 is answered by AC2.
- **Completeness:** `## Acceptance Criteria` is present and the `## Key Files` paths are syntactically valid; all 11 referenced files exist at HEAD (`7bfe98f`).
- **Sequencing & dependencies:** no children. This item is the prerequisite (epic child #1) for boss integration (child #6) and the parity guard (child #10). Tests are embedded in AC1–AC5, so the test-first intent is satisfied without separate children.
- **Scope sizing:** one focused refactor (add `_tickPlayer`, migrate six scenes, tests, docs) — a deliverable increment.
- **Acceptance & testability:** all ACs are pass/fail; AC3 (cross-scene equivalence) and AC5 (duplicate-body guard) name automated verification.
- **Polish & handoff:** description is actionable; the Key Files list matches the consumer set.
- **AC coverage review:** `run_coverage_review` returned `recommendation: proceed` (leaf item; no children).

## Plan — clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: "OQ8 — should `GymPlayer` (bare-bones tuning scene) consume the shared control step, or stay minimal?" Answer (epic `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`): *Recommended: consume the shared input/physics helper; it need not add enemies.* Final accepted: **yes** — AC2 requires `GymPlayer` to consume the shared input mapping.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Is the sequence described in the summary actually one identical sequence in every named scene?" Research (HEAD `7bfe98f`; read of `PlayScene.tick` L557–572, `GymFormationScene.tick` L1299–1318, `GymWeapons.tick` L178–195, `GymPowerUpsUtility.tick` L154–170, `GymPowerUpsCombat.tick` L258–275): the scenes run **subsets with different ordering**, not identical copies — `PlayScene` runs tickWeaponTimers → multipliers → `_handleTeleport` → input → physics → auto-fire; `GymFormationScene` runs timers → multipliers → input → physics → auto-fire with teleport later; `GymWeapons` omits the P5 multipliers; `GymPowerUpsUtility` omits tickWeaponTimers and auto-fire; `GymPowerUpsCombat` omits timers, multipliers and auto-fire. Resolution (epic assumption, "the shipped game is canonical"): the shared `_tickPlayer(dt)` runs the full ordered sequence and each gym's absent feature resolves to a no-op (multiplier 1, empty weapon list). Recorded as an implementation assumption; if a test shows a behaviour change in those gyms the difference must be recorded in the epic and approved.
- Q (self-directed, repo research): "Does `GymPowerUpsCombat` use a fake fixed 16 ms clock for the *player* path (AC4)?" Research: the only fixed 16 ms step is `_nextFireTime += 16` inside `_tickScouts` (`GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` L424), which is the **enemy-fire** clock and belongs to epic child #2 (`AH-0MUII3BBW000XZ46`, "Shared enemy-fire dispatch using the real scene clock"); the player path already advances from the supplied `dt`. **OPEN QUESTION (AC4 wording):** AC4 should be read as "the `GymPowerUpsCombat` player path uses the supplied `dt`" (already true); the 16 ms enemy clock is fixed by child #2, not by this item. Intent is clear enough to implement; the wording is flagged for correction rather than rewritten here (rewriting could change intent).

**OQ-NOTE (effort/risk):** the autoplan pre-check generated a zeroed placeholder estimate (O=M=P=0, 0.00 h → Extra Small / Low) because `plan_helpers.run_effort_and_risk` submits a fixed `{o:0,m:0,p:0}` payload. Treat the `effort`/`risk` fields as a placeholder; `<WIP-id>` should receive a genuine `/skill:effort-and-risk` estimate before implementation is dispatched.

# Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge

## Problem statement

Replace the game's hand-rolled procedural Web Audio synthesis (~2,253 lines in `src/audio/effects.ts`) with **ToneForge** (`../ToneForge`) — build-time rendered WAV assets consumed via Phaser. All SFX are produced through one dedicated audio toolchain, ensuring reproducible, seed-deterministic output.

## Decision: Baked assets (approach A)

**Chosen approach: Build-time baked WAV assets.** ToneForge CLI renders each cue to a WAV file during a build step, consumed by Phaser at runtime. This matches ToneForge's documented game-dev workflow, keeps the browser dependency surface clean (no Node-only deps leaking into the game bundle), and is the simplest integration path.

**Trade-off:** Runtime variation (pitch jitter, thrust-driven hum) is lost in baked form. These are handled separately:
- Thruster hum: baked multiple variants or played via a lightweight Tone.js shim at runtime (to be evaluated in a follow-up work item).
- Pitch jitter: baked multiple variants with different seeds to approximate variation.

**Child work items created:**
- Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (browser-compatible) — sibling work item in `../ToneForge`
- Consider switching to runtime generation when possible — child work item here
- Update ToneForge license to MIT — sibling work item in `../ToneForge`

## Users

- **Game developer (primary):** Wants a single, well-documented audio toolchain with deterministic output, easy recipe authoring, and reproducible builds.

### User stories

- As the game's developer, I want every SFX cue produced via ToneForge so that audio is authored, generated and varied reproducibly with one toolchain.
- As the game's developer, I want the build pipeline to render all WAV assets in CI so that the game bundle is self-contained and reproducible.
- As the game's developer, I want to author new recipes in ToneForge without modifying game audio code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Approach recorded:** Baked assets (A) approach is chosen with rationale; any required ToneForge changes are split into child work items (runtime-awareness, licence update, future runtime consideration).
- **Cue-to-recipe mapping:** Every cue exported by `src/audio/effects.ts` today is mapped to a ToneForge recipe/stack/sequence (existing or newly authored) or explicitly retired, documented on this item.
- **Recipes available to ToneForge:** Any newly authored recipes/presets are data-only ToneGraph/preset files authored in AI_Hell under `audio/toneforge/` and made resolvable to the pinned ToneForge CLI via its external recipe directory (`TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR`); each is documented (name, character, seed). Recipe files are not committed into `../ToneForge`.
- **Audible character preserved (verification step):** The audible character of each retained cue matches GDD §7.3 (waveform family, frequency contour and nominal volume preserved within audible similarity), verified by the explicit audible-character audition step in Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51).
- **Global volume/mute:** `setSfxVolume`/`setSfxMuted` continues to affect all cues; SettingsScene controls still work.
- **Single shared context:** Exactly one shared `AudioContext` is created; a new scene/cue does not construct a second context (invariant asserted in tests).
- **No-op when unavailable:** In an environment without an `AudioContext`, every cue degrades to a no-op and never throws (verified by headless tests).
- **Advance cues ≥ 500 ms:** Advance cues remain ≥ 500 ms and cue→fire scheduling remains gap-free where required.
- **Deterministic build:** Rendering is seed-deterministic, checksums are recorded, and the generation step is reproducible in CI.
- **Pinned dependency:** ToneForge is consumed reproducibly (`file:` dependency to sibling checkout, pinned to a commit or tag); the build must not silently depend on an unpinned checkout.
- **No Node-only deps in browser:** Node-only ToneForge dependencies do not leak into the browser game bundle.
- **Tests and build pass:** Full test suite passes (`npm test`), and `npm run build` / `npm run typecheck` pass clean.
- **Documentation updated:** GDD §7.3, the audio-directory tree note and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` describe the ToneForge-based pipeline.

## Constraints

- GDD §7.3 currently mandates "zero external audio assets" — the baked approach changes this stance; the GDD must be updated to reflect build-time generation.
- ToneForge is v0.1.0; API may change. Pin to a specific commit/tag.
- ToneForge license must be resolved (MIT — child work item in sibling repo).
- Build-time generation must be reproducible (deterministic seeds, checksums).
- The thruster hum is continuous and thrust-driven — may need a runtime shim or multiple baked variants.

## Existing state

- ~2,253 lines of procedural Web Audio in `src/audio/effects.ts`
- Consumers import cue functions directly from `../audio/effects`
- ToneForge sibling checkout at `../ToneForge` (commit `c48fed5`, MIT license — TBD in repo)
- ToneForge CLI: `toneforge`/`tf`, commands include `generate`, `show`, `list recipes`, `sequence`, `stack`, `explore`, `play`
- Recipe catalogue is card-game oriented; only `weapon-laser-zap` is game-action relevant

## Desired change

- Build pipeline step renders all game cues to WAV via ToneForge CLI
- Phaser plays WAV files instead of procedural synthesis
- New recipes/presets authored in ToneForge for game cues
- SettingsScene volume/mute controls wired to Phaser audio node
- Tests updated to assert ToneForge-based behaviour

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Replace procedural synthesis with Phaser audio playback
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Update tests for ToneForge-based cues
- `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` — Update master tests
- `../ToneForge/src/recipes/` — Add game recipe definitions
- `../ToneForge/presets/` — Add game presets
- `scripts/build-audio.sh` (new) — Build step to render WAVs via ToneForge CLI
- `public/audio/sfx/` (new directory) — Baked WAV assets
- `package.json` — Add `file:` dependency on ToneForge
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — Update audio direction
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Update per-enemy audio

## Related work

- Cross-repo prerequisite (ToneForge Worklog): Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (browser-compatible playback) (TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0) — supersedes deleted AI_Hell child AH-0MUTVP8600019HFO.
- Cross-repo prerequisite (ToneForge Worklog): Update ToneForge licence to MIT (TF-0MUTVQSI6003VPAD) — supersedes deleted AI_Hell child AH-0MUTVVAL1002AY12.
- Child work items here: cue-to-recipe mapping, recipe authoring, build pipeline, contract tests, effects.ts rewrite, thruster shim, documentation, pin/bundle hygiene, and the runtime-generation evaluation.
- References: GDD §7.3 (Audio Direction), ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md
- ToneForge sibling repo: `../ToneForge`

## Plan

Planning review completed 2026-10-04 (auto-complete path: effort Medium, risk High). The existing decomposition was reviewed and augmented rather than regenerated.

### Child work items (dependency order)

1. **Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit** (AH-0MUTYV7SQ005HURT) — no dependencies.
2. **Add CLI command to register new primitive recipes** (TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18, ToneForge Worklog) — prerequisite for game-specific recipe authoring; enables external recipe registration via CLI.
3. **Author game-specific ToneForge recipes** (AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51) — depends on cue mapping and CLI registration command (TF-0MUUC9RTU008UJ18).
4. **Audio playback contract tests** (AH-0MUTYV8RJ009MWKJ) — depends on cue mapping. Test-first: written before the rewrite.
5. **Deterministic WAV build pipeline** (AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD) — depends on recipe authoring.
6. **Rewrite effects.ts to Phaser playback** (AH-0MUTYV92Y000WJ8Z) — depends on the build pipeline and contract tests.
7. **Thruster hum Tone.js shim** (AH-0MUTYV9ES003A3HJ) — depends on the contract tests and the rewrite.
8. **Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene** (AH-0MUTYVA2C000SNPO) — depends on the rewrite and the licence update.
9. **Update audio documentation** (AH-0MUTYV9QV0000HDT) — depends on cue mapping, recipe authoring and the build pipeline.
10. **Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (browser-compatible playback)** (TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0, ToneForge Worklog) — cross-repo prerequisite; no in-repo dependencies. (The former AI_Hell child AH-0MUTVP8600019HFO was deleted after recreation in ToneForge.)
11. **Update ToneForge licence to MIT** (TF-0MUTVQSI6003VPAD, ToneForge Worklog) — cross-repo prerequisite; blocks bundle hygiene/licence resolution.
12. **Evaluate switching to runtime generation when ToneForge is Runtime-ready** (AH-0MUTVQDH2008DEF6) — depends on runtime-awareness (now the cross-repo item TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0); evaluative only, no ToneForge code changes required.

### Vertical slice phasing

Each implementation child is an end-to-end increment (code + tests + docs/infra where applicable): cue mapping (discovery) → CLI registration command (prerequisite) → recipe authoring (assets) → contract tests (executable requirements) → build pipeline (assets + CI) → rewrite (runtime playback) → thruster shim (continuous hum) → pin/hygiene (reproducibility) → documentation (handoff). Between phases, review the next item's description before starting it.

### Resolved producer decisions (2026-10-04)

- **Cross-repo scheduling.** Producer decision: Make ToneForge Runtime-aware and Update ToneForge licence to MIT are owned in the ToneForge Worklog. Runtime-awareness was recreated as TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0; the AI_Hell child AH-0MUTVP8600019HFO was deleted. The licence change is tracked as TF-0MUTVQSI6003VPAD. Evaluate switching to runtime generation (AH-0MUTVQDH2008DEF6) remains here and treats TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0 as an external prerequisite. Dependency edges cannot span Worklogs, so the AI_Hell `blocked` status auto-recomputes to `open`; the item is instead guarded with the `do-not-delegate` tag so it is not auto-dispatched before the prerequisite completes.
- **Audible-character verification (AC4).** Producer decision: add a verification step. An explicit audible-character audition acceptance criterion was added to Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51), and AC4 now cites it.
- **Parent AC format.** Producer decision: reformat. The epic acceptance criteria are now a `- ` bullet list, parseable by `tree_coverage.py`.
- **Recipe authoring location (recommended by operator).** Producer believes Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51) does not require changes in `../ToneForge`. Evidence gathered (see comment): `tf generate --recipe` resolves names only from the ToneForge recipe registry, which registers built-in code recipes plus file-backed ToneGraph files discovered from `../ToneForge/presets/recipes/` (the discovery directory is not overridable by env var or CLI). Composite cues can be expressed as stack/sequence preset JSON files rendered via `tf stack render --preset <path>` / `tf sequence render --preset <path>`, which can live in AI_Hell. # Author game-specific ToneForge recipes

## Goal

Author the game-specific recipes identified by the cue-to-recipe mapping task, so every non-retired game cue has a deterministic, seed-documented recipe that can be rendered to WAV.

As the game's developer, I want to author new recipes without modifying game audio code.

## Resolved authoring mechanism (2026-10-05)

The producer delegated the mechanism choice; **mechanism (b) external recipe directory** was chosen. Recipes are authored as **data-only ToneGraph YAML inside AI_Hell** and made resolvable to a fresh `tf generate` process via ToneForge's external recipe-directory capability (`TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR` / `tf library add --destination`). No files inside `../ToneForge` are edited by this item.

Rationale (full record in the epic AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J and this item's comments):

- `../ToneForge/presets/recipes/` would require a cross-repo commit that the AI_Hell implement worktree workflow cannot make.
- Composing only from existing primitives is impossible: `../ToneForge/src/core/tonegraph-schema.ts` drops `automation` entirely, so no frequency contour is expressible in a file-backed recipe.

This supersedes the earlier scope text that referenced `../ToneForge/src/recipes/`.

## Scope

- Author one ToneGraph YAML recipe per `new-recipe` slug under `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-*.yaml` in this repo (seed block 32100–32199), expressing the character from the cue-to-recipe mapping via data-only ToneGraph (`oscillator`, `noise`, `biquadFilter`, `envelope`, `gain`, `automation`).
- For composite cues (e.g. player hull breach = thump + body + HP-noise tail; victory fanfare; defeat sting), compose stack/sequence preset JSON under `audio/toneforge/presets/` referencing primitive recipes rather than duplicating synthesis.
- Register/locate the directory for rendering via ToneForge's external recipe-directory mechanism (`TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR`).
- Document each recipe (name, audible character, recommended seed) in `audio/toneforge/README.md` (and the audio docs child).
- Verify each recipe renders deterministically: `tf generate --recipe <slug> --seed <n>` twice yields byte-identical bytes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every `new-recipe` row from the cue-to-recipe mapping task exists as a data-only recipe/preset file in this repo.
- Every new recipe renders a non-empty WAV via `tf generate` with its reserved seed.
- Re-rendering the same recipe with the same seed produces byte-identical output (determinism verified).
- Composite cues are composed from existing/primitive recipes; any new primitive is itself covered by the render/determinism checks.
- Each recipe is documented with name, audible character and recommended seed.
- The recipe directory is resolvable by a fresh `tf generate` process via the external recipe-directory mechanism (no edits inside `../ToneForge`).
- `npm test` passes in this repo (the recipe files are exercised through the audio build/contract tests).
- Audible-character audition (verification step): each newly authored recipe is auditioned against its GDD §7.3 character description (waveform family, frequency contour, nominal volume); the audition result is recorded on this work item and verifies parent epic AC4.

## Dependencies

- Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit — completed (produces the required recipe slug list).
- **TF-0MUV8YKFR002BIA2** (ToneForge Worklog) — frequency-ramp / `automation` support for file-backed recipes. **External prerequisite; must be terminal.**
- **TF-0MUVC3DZ10089SAU** (ToneForge Worklog) — allow external tools to register recipes via CLI (persistent / external directory, `TONEFORGE_RECIPE_DIR`). **External prerequisite; must be terminal.**
- Sequencing guard: this item is tagged `do-not-delegate` and must not be auto-dispatched before both external prerequisites are terminal (producer-confirmed 2026-10-05).

## Deliverables

- Data-only recipe YAML files: `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-*.yaml`.
- Composite presets: `audio/toneforge/presets/*.json`.
- Recipe documentation: `audio/toneforge/README.md`.
- Determinism evidence (byte-identical re-render) recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `audio/toneforge/presets/` — new composite presets (created by this item).

# Deterministic WAV build pipeline

## Goal

Create a build step that renders every game recipe to baked WAV assets under `public/audio/sfx/` via the ToneForge CLI, with recorded checksums, so the game bundle is self-contained and the generation step is reproducible in CI.

As the game's developer, I want the build pipeline to render all WAV assets in CI so that the game bundle is self-contained and reproducible.

## Scope

- Add `scripts/build-audio.sh` that iterates the game recipe manifest, invokes `tf generate --recipe <slug> --seed <n> --output public/audio/sfx/<name>.wav`, and fails fast on any render error.
- Emit `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` (SHA-256 per asset) after a successful render.
- Add an `npm run build-audio` script and wire it into `npm run build` as a preceding step.
- Add a reproducibility check: re-rendering with the same seeds must reproduce identical checksums; drift fails the script.
- Add a CI step that runs `npm run build-audio` and fails if generated assets differ from the committed checksums.
- Handle pitch-jitter variants (explosions) by rendering a small fixed set of seeds and selecting among them at runtime.
- Thruster hum is out of scope for baking (handled by the runtime shim task).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `npm run build-audio` renders all manifest recipes to `public/audio/sfx/` and exits non-zero on any failure.
- `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` records a SHA-256 for every rendered asset.
- Re-running `npm run build-audio` with unchanged seeds produces an identical `checksums.json`.
- `npm run build` invokes the audio build before the Vite bundle step.
- CI fails when a rendered asset's checksum does not match the committed manifest.
- The script's recipe manifest is a single source of truth consumed by both the build and the tests.
- No Node-only ToneForge dependency is bundled into the browser output (verified by build inspection).

## Dependencies

- Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (must exist before they can be rendered).

## Deliverables

- `scripts/build-audio.sh`.
- Recipe manifest file consumed by the script.
- `public/audio/sfx/` baked WAV assets plus `checksums.json`.
- `package.json` `build-audio` script and `build` wiring.
- CI job step invoking the build and verifying checksums.

## Key Files

- `scripts/build-audio.sh` — new build script.
- `package.json` — `build-audio` and `build` scripts.
- `public/audio/sfx/` — baked asset output directory.
- `../ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js` — `tf`/`toneforge` CLI entry point.

# Thruster hum Tone.js shim

## Goal

Implement the continuous, thrust-driven thruster hum as a lightweight Tone.js runtime shim, since baked WAV variants cannot reproduce a pitch/gain-continuous, thrust-coupled loop.

As the game's developer, I want the thruster hum to remain continuous and thrust-driven, so the tuning slider stays audible and the hum stays in lockstep with the flame animation.

## Scope

- Add a small Tone.js-based runtime shim that owns only the thruster hum; all other cues are baked assets (decision recorded on the parent epic).
- Preserve the existing `updateThrusterSound(level)` / `stopThrusterSound()` contract consumed by `Player.preUpdate`.
- Reproduce the documented character: triangle fundamental ~60 Hz + sine undertone ~35 Hz + band-pass filtered noise (700–1100 Hz) whoosh, gain ≤ 0.075.
- Mirror the flame growth/shrink timing (30 ms growth, ~4x decay) and avoid clicks on retrigger.
- Stop cleanly on release, respawn, player destroy and scene shutdown so no audio nodes leak.
- Degrade to a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- Add Tone.js as a pinned runtime dependency and verify it is the only new browser runtime dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The thruster hum is continuous while thrust is held and stops cleanly on release/respawn/destroy/scene shutdown.
- Hum gain tracks `getEngineSoundLevel` and stays ≤ 0.075.
- No clicks on retrigger; growth/decay match the documented flame timing.
- The shim is a safe no-op without an `AudioContext`.
- No audio nodes leak after repeated thrust start/stop cycles (asserted in tests).
- Tone.js is pinned and is the only new browser runtime dependency introduced.
- `npm test`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` pass.

## Dependencies

- Audio playback contract tests.
- Rewrite effects.ts to Phaser playback.

## Deliverables

- Thruster hum shim module.
- Wiring from `updateThrusterSound`/`stopThrusterSound` to the shim.

# Intake Brief — Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 periodic bomb (range/frequency) level axes into the effect path (AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB)

**Headline:** Wire the P3 `shieldAbsorptions` axis into the effect path (a levelled
shield absorbs N hits before popping) and **redesign P4** from a one-shot
charged clear into a **range-and-frequency levelled bomb** that is a single
explosion on a field pickup and a permanent periodic clear when chosen as a
hold-full reward — identically in `PlayScene` and every gym.

**Status:** intake complete — producer decisions recorded (see Appendix). This
brief **supersedes** the original P4 `bombCharges` design from
AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6: P4 has **no charges**; its level axes are now
`bombRange` (px) and `bombFrequency` (pulses/s).

## Problem statement

The shipped power-up level catalogue (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent
AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) defines P3 `shieldAbsorptions` (1 → 3, k=0.5) and a P4
axis, but the effect path never consumes them:

- **P3** is a single-hit shield — `EffectsRegistry.tryAbsorbShield()` deletes
  P3 on the first absorb, so the levelled axis changes nothing in play.
- **P4** is instant and stateless — `CombatCoreScene._collectDrop()` calls
  `_clearEnemyBullets()` immediately and stores no state, so a levelled axis
  changes nothing in play.

Because the hold-full choice can offer a `power-up-level` for P3/P4, its
change summary (`summarisePowerUpLevelChange`) can currently promise a delta
that the effect path never applies. The producer has now **changed the P4
design**: instead of banked charges, P4 clears all enemy bullets within a
radius, and levelling increases that **range** and the **frequency** with
which it fires (permanently when granted by a hold-full pick).

## Users

- **Player (shield progression):** "As a player, when my shield is levelled, it
  should absorb the promised number of hits before popping — not always one."
- **Player (bomb progression):** "As a player, a levelled bomb should clear a
  larger area and (when permanent) pulse more often, with a single explosion
  from a field pickup and an ongoing periodic clear from a hold-full pick."
- **Player (trustworthy choice):** "As a player, the change summary on a
  power-up level-up must be the change I actually see."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — P3 multi-hit absorption.** `EffectsRegistry` tracks a run-scoped
  remaining-absorptions count resolved from `store.stats('P3').shieldAbsorptions`;
  a shield active at upgrade level L absorbs exactly that many hits before
  popping, and behaves as today (exactly 1 hit) at level 0. The shield remains
  a single activation whose remaining count is refreshed (never added) on a
  new P3 collection; the run-scoped **level** still persists after the bubble
  expires.
- **AC2 — P4 field pickup is a single explosion.** A field-collected P4
  immediately destroys every enemy bullet within the resolved `bombRange`
  (px, centred on the player) exactly once and is then gone; it stores no
  persistent state. Bullets only — no enemy damage.
- **AC3 — P4 hold-full reward is a permanent periodic clear.** A hold-full /
  permanent P4 fires immediately and then clears enemy bullets within the
  resolved `bombRange` every `1 / bombFrequency` seconds for the rest of the
  run; it never expires, is unaffected by activation timeouts, and is cleared
  only by `reset()`.
- **AC4 — P4 level axes replace charges.** `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.P4` exposes
  `bombRange` (base 120 px → cap 320 px, k=0.3) and `bombFrequency`
  (base 0.33 /s → cap 1 /s, k=0.35); `bombCharges` is removed from the
  variable space, stats interface and resolver output. Both axes are monotonic
  non-decreasing and clamped to their caps; range is resolved live so a
  level-up mid-run enlarges subsequent pulses.
- **AC5 — Choice-summary truthfulness.** After wiring, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`
  no longer defers P3/P4 (`DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES` becomes empty);
  a `power-up-level` offer for P3 or P4 whose summary promises a delta results
  in a measurable behaviour change (multi-hit absorb count; bomb range/frequency).
- **AC6 — Parity + reset.** Identical P3/P4 behaviour in `PlayScene` and every
  gym that applies them (shared `EffectsRegistry` / `CombatCoreScene` code, the
  duplicate-body guard passes); remaining P3 absorptions, the P4 permanent flag
  and the P4 pulse timer are run-scoped and cleared by `reset()`.
- **AC7 — HUD feedback.** The active P3 effect row shows the remaining
  absorptions (e.g. `Shield ×2`), and a permanent P4 is listed as an active
  effect; both update as hits are absorbed / the level changes.
- **AC8 — Tests.** Unit + parity tests cover: multi-hit absorb counts per P3
  level; level-0 single-hit backward compatibility; P4 field single-pulse and
  consumption; P4 permanent immediate + interval pulses with per-level range;
  reset semantics; level persistence across timeouts; choice-summary
  truthfulness; and game↔gym equality (including the `CombatScene`
  duplicate-body guard).
- **AC9 — Docs.** GDD §4.4 and §4.4.3 (P3 description, P4 row/table, and the
  "P3/P4 consumption deferred" bullet) and the relevant code comments are
  updated to describe the P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/
  `bombFrequency` axes as wired; the superseded `bombCharges` design is
  removed.
- **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**
- **AC11 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** the pulsing/absorption mechanism must run
  the **same code** in the game and every gym. Registry-level state and the
  shared `CombatCoreScene` pulse path are the single source; no per-scene
  copies. Enforced by `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- **Model invariants:** level variables must be monotonic non-decreasing and
  clamped to a finite cap (`src/utils/curve.ts`). `bombFrequency` is therefore
  stored as pulses/second; the effect computes the interval as `1 / frequency`.
- **No charges:** P4 must not introduce or retain a charge counter.
- **Scope:** the blast clears **enemy bullets only** (no enemy damage), centred
  on the player; no new P4 enemy-damage behaviour.
- **Reset semantics:** P3 remaining absorptions and P4 permanent/pulse state are
  run-scoped and cleared by `EffectsRegistry.reset()` / `CombatCoreScene.resetRunState()`.
- Balance changes beyond the Q2=A values are out of scope.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS.P4` currently holds
  `bombCharges` (base 1 → cap 3, k=0.5); `PowerUpLevelStats.bombCharges`;
  `DEFERRED_POWER_UP_LEVEL_VARIABLES = { shieldAbsorptions, bombCharges }`
  excludes both from the summariser.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `tryAbsorbShield()` deletes P3 on the first hit;
  `_applyTimedEffect` has no P4 branch ("no registry-local timed state"); the
  file comment documents both axes as deferred.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_collectDrop()` calls
  `_clearEnemyBullets()` immediately for `drop.dropId === 'P4'`;
  `_clearEnemyBullets()` clears every enemy bullet with no range filter;
  `onPowerUpCollected()` shows the shared `BombNotice`.
- `src/scenes/core/BombNotice.ts` — shared "BOMB! Bullets cleared" notice.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` + `EffectsRegistry.getActiveEffects()` — the single HUD row
  builder (P3 currently has no remaining-hits field).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 / §4.4.3 — describes the deferred axes
  and the `bombCharges` P4 row.

## Desired change

1. **P3:** add run-scoped `_shieldRemaining` state to `EffectsRegistry`. On
   `applyCollect('P3', …)` resolve `shieldAbsorptions` and set (refresh) the
   remaining count alongside the timed duration. `tryAbsorbShield()` decrements
   and keeps the shield while `remaining > 0`, popping on the last hit. Reset
   clears it. Expose `shieldAbsorptionsRemaining()` for the HUD.
2. **P4 model:** replace the `bombCharges` spec/stats with `bombRange` and
   `bombFrequency` (Q2=A values); remove `bombCharges` from the variable
   space, `PowerUpLevelStats`, the resolver and the deferred set; update the
   summariser so P3/P4 deltas are no longer excluded.
3. **P4 effect:** add registry state for the permanent periodic pulse (active
   flag + seconds-to-next-pulse) and a single-pulse request for field pickups.
   The shared core drives a new ranged clear (`_clearEnemyBulletsInRange(x, y,
   range)`) from the registry each frame; field pickups fire once, permanent
   P4 fires immediately then on the resolved interval. Remove the P4
   `BombNotice` show path (producer Q3) and render an expanding-ring VFX at the
   cleared radius instead.
4. **HUD:** surface P3 remaining absorptions in its row and P4 (permanent) as an
   active effect.
5. **Docs/tests:** update GDD and code comments; add the AC8 coverage.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — replace the P4 spec/axis; empty the deferred set.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` — P4 range/frequency specs, resolver, removed `bombCharges`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — P3 remaining-absorptions state; P4 single-pulse/permanent pulse state; active-effect HUD data.
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — absorb counts, field vs permanent P4, reset, level persistence.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — ranged bullet clear; drive P4 pulses from the registry; drop the P4 `BombNotice` call.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — shield absorption path (`tryAbsorbPlayerHit`) unchanged contract, multi-hit aware.
- `src/scenes/core/BombNotice.ts` — retire/stop using the P4 notice (producer Q3=A).
- `src/vfx/aoeEffect.ts` (or a new P4 pulse VFX) — expanding-ring visual at the cleared radius.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — P3 remaining-hits display; P4 active row.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts`, gym parity tests, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 / §4.4.3 P3 + P4 updates.

## Assumptions

- "Timed for a single explosion" for a field pickup is read as a **one-shot**
  (immediate, per Q3=A) explosion that is consumed, not a fuse delay — the
  producer gave no fuse duration.
- The pulse is centred on the **player ship** and clears **enemy bullets only**.
- `bombFrequency` is expressed in pulses per second to keep the model monotonic
  non-decreasing; the interval is its reciprocal.
- The hold-full `power-up-level` offer applies via `applyCollect(id, true)`
  (permanent), so a promised P4 frequency delta is observable.

## Risks

- **Balance (P4):** a permanent 1/s, 320 px clear could trivialise bullet-hell
  phases. *Mitigation:* conservative caps with a written rationale in the spec;
  values remain catalogue-driven and tunable.
- **Model change:** removing `bombCharges` touches the catalogue, stats,
  resolver, deferred set, tests and GDD. *Mitigation:* single change, grep for
  every `bombCharges` reference; the model test suite enforces completeness.
- **Parity drift:** a range filter or pulse timer implemented per-scene would
  diverge game vs gyms. *Mitigation:* keep both in `EffectsRegistry` /
  `CombatCoreScene`; the duplicate-body guard fails otherwise.
- **Scope creep:** HUD treatment and VFX can expand. *Mitigation:* limit to the
  stated AC7 HUD fields and a single expanding-ring VFX; record extra
  opportunities as linked work items.
- **P3 refresh semantics:** refreshing (not stacking) remaining absorptions is a
  design call; documented in AC1 and tested.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Power-up level curve design + catalogue + pure
  resolver (P4 `bombCharges` design, now superseded for P4 by this item).
- **AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Wired the level model into `EffectsRegistry`; its
  producer decision Q2=B deferred P3 `shieldAbsorptions` / P4 `bombCharges`
  consumption to this item.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** — Hold-full `power-up-level` choice integration
  (`summarisePowerUpLevelChange` truthfulness).
- **AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR** — Power-up level gym demonstration/parity suite.
- `src/scenes/core/BombNotice.ts` (AH-0MU8QVH3A009RS1G / AH-0MUII3CXX0023H24) —
  the P4 notice this item stops using.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** – Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed)
- **AH-0MTE8EBG3004QC66** – Combat gym scene: GymPowerUpsCombat with ship, scouts, spawner, effects (completed)
- **AH-0MUQFXDKF005NM9N** – [test-failure] src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts > PlayScene — boss encounter test (completed)

Repository files matching: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Once collected, should the P4 pulse be a retained ability or a timed effect?" — Options A permanent run-scoped, B timed window, C hybrid. **Recommended A.** Answer (producer): *field pickup = timed for a single explosion (once it explodes it is gone); hold-full purchase = permanent.* → Resolved as a **hybrid**: field pickup is a one-shot explosion, hold-full is permanent/periodic (AC2/AC3). Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Curve values for the two new axes (range px, frequency /s)?" — **Recommended A** (range 120→320 px, k=0.3; frequency 0.33→1 /s, k=0.35). Answer (producer): *A*. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "First pulse and VFX?" — **Recommended A** (immediate pulse on collect; ring VFX; reuse notice). Answer (producer): *A — remove the "BOMB!" notice.* → Immediate pulse adopted; the shared `BombNotice` is removed from the P4 path. Source: interactive reply.
- Q4 (P4 directive, superseding the original charges design): "How should P4 behave?" — Answer (producer): *"Change the behaviour of P4: it should fire periodically destroying all bullets within a given range. There should be no 'charges'. As the weapon is levelled up it will increase range and frequency."* → Drives AC2–AC5 and the catalogue change. Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief — Level-up offers duplicate weapon (basic + upgraded version of same weapon) (AH-0MUVRACE9001WVT2)

**Headline:** The hold-full choice overlay can offer the same item twice — its
base-pool entry (e.g. "Spread Shot") *and* a levelled-up entry (e.g. "Spread
Shot Lv.3") — because `buildChoiceCandidates` emits both unconditionally for any
owned weapon/power-up. Suppress the base-pool entry once the item is owned so a
single, correctly-labelled upgrade offer remains.

## Problem statement

Sometimes, when the mineral hold fills and the level-up choice opens, the player
is offered both a **basic** and an **upgraded** version of the same weapon — for
example "Spread Shot" *and* "Spread Shot Lv.3". The two options look different
but are functionally identical: both permanently equip the weapon and raise its
run-scoped level by one. The result is a confusing, wasteful choice screen.

### Verified root cause

`buildChoiceCandidates` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) builds the candidate list as:

1. the **base pool** (`CHOICE_POOL` — P3–P10 plus `spread`, `dual`, `rapid`,
   `nova`, `mortar`, `arc`), each emitted as `kind: 'weapon'` / `'powerup'`; and
2. one `kind: 'weapon-level'` (`'power-up-level'`) offer per **owned** item from
   `ChoiceContext.weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels`.

An owned weapon therefore appears **twice**. When either entry is chosen,
`applyMineralChoiceReward` (`src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`) runs the *same*
path — `effectsRegistry.applyWeapon(id, true)` + `player.equipWeapon(id, true)`
— granting the weapon permanently and incrementing its level by one.

The bug is **not** specific to temporary drops or to the absence of a permanent
grant: it reproduces for *any* item the player has ever collected this run,
because `Player.getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` return all run-scoped
levels (which persist across timed expiry, by design). The reporter's "two
temporary Spread Shot upgrades with no permanent" is one instance, not the
trigger. The same duplication exists for power-ups.

The existing tests mask it: `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` asserts
option distinctness keyed on `${kind}:${id}`, so `weapon:spread` and
`weapon-level:spread` count as "distinct".

## Users and user stories

- **Player (clear choice):** "As a player at a hold-full level-up, I want each
  weapon or power-up to appear **once**, at its true upgrade level, so I can
  tell my options apart and never waste a pick on two identical offers."
- **Player (correct labels):** "As a player, when I already own Spread Shot at
  level 2, I want the offer to read 'Spread Shot Lv.3', not a bare 'Spread Shot'
  that secretly does the same thing."
- **Designer/tuner:** "As a designer, I want the candidate pool to hold one
  entry per offered item so the three slots are never spent on duplicates."
- **Developer:** "As a developer, I want the de-duplication in one shared place
  (`buildChoiceCandidates`) so the game and every gym behave identically."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No duplicate weapon offers.** When a weapon is owned (run-scoped level
  ≥ 1), the candidate list contains **no** `kind: 'weapon'` entry for that id —
  only the `kind: 'weapon-level'` entry, labelled with the level it grants. An
  **unowned** weapon still produces exactly one base-pool `kind: 'weapon'` entry
  with its **New** badge.
- **AC2 — No duplicate power-up offers.** The same rule applies to power-ups:
  an owned power-up (level ≥ 1) produces only its `kind: 'power-up-level'`
  entry; an unowned power-up keeps its single base-pool `kind: 'powerup'` entry
  and **New** badge.
- **AC3 — Single shared implementation + parity.** The de-duplication lives once
  in `buildChoiceCandidates` (`src/powerups/choice.ts`) and is consumed by the
  game (`PlayScene`) and every gym launcher, with no divergent copy. The
  `GymWeaponLeveling` custom selection strategy keeps guaranteeing a
  `weapon-level` offer while no longer being able to pick a duplicate base/level
  pair.
- **AC4 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover: owned vs unowned weapons;
  owned vs unowned power-ups; the candidate list never containing both a base
  and a level-up entry for the same id; and the base pool being unchanged when
  nothing is owned. At least one integration-level test asserts that a real
  draw (via the default strategy with a real `ChoiceContext`) never yields two
  options that apply the same underlying item.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and the Game Design Document §4.5
  hold-full-choice wording (which currently says the pool is "extended with" a
  level-up offer — it must also state the base entry is suppressed once owned).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Persistent-level semantics unchanged.** This is a *presentation/candidate*
  fix only. The existing rule that every collection raises the run-scoped level
  and that the level persists across a timed expiry
  (AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J AC2; AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9) is **not** modified.
- **Keep the 3-offer mechanism.** The overlay still offers three distinct
  options; the change is which candidates exist, not how many are drawn.
- **Backward compatibility.** `ChoiceOption` and the `ChoiceStrategy` contract
  stay source-compatible; existing strategies keep working.
- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** Shared behaviour stays in
  `src/powerups/choice.ts`; gyms that open the choice are updated/verified in
  the same change, and the duplicate-body/equivalence guard must stay green.
- **Run-scoped only.** No leaderboard or persistence impact.

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `CHOICE_POOL`, `ChoiceOption`, `ChoiceContext`,
  `isWeaponDrop`, `toChoiceOption`, `buildChoiceCandidates`,
  `createRandomChoiceStrategy`. `buildChoiceCandidates` maps the whole pool to
  base entries first, then **appends** level-up entries; it never removes a base
  entry for an owned id. It already computes `ownedWeapons`/`ownedPowerUps` sets
  (used only for the **New** badge).
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — `applyMineralChoiceReward` applies a
  base-pool `weapon`/`powerup` entry and a `weapon-level`/`power-up-level` entry
  through the same permanent path, confirming they are duplicates in effect.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` return
  every owned item (level > 0), i.e. the ownership source for the fix.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — renders `option.name`, the **New** badge
  and the `changeSummary`; no change expected.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` — custom strategy that filters
  `weapon-level` entries out of the base pool and de-duplicates by
  `(id, kind)`; must remain correct after the base entry is suppressed.
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — the tests that currently encode the
  duplicate as "distinct"; the section asserting the base-pool entry is present
  for an owned weapon (`does not mark a weapon as New when the player owns it`)
  will need updating to assert its **absence** (only when owned).

## Desired change

In `buildChoiceCandidates`, when building the base-pool candidates, **skip** a
`weapon`/`powerup` entry whose id is present in `ownedWeapons`/`ownedPowerUps`
(ownership is already computed there). Level-up offers continue to be appended
exactly as today. Net effect: each owned item is offered once, as its levelled
offer; each unowned item is offered once, as a **New** base entry.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — suppress the base-pool candidate for an owned
  weapon/power-up id in `buildChoiceCandidates`; update the function's doc
  comment.
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — update the "not New when owned"
  cases to assert absence of the base entry; add owned/unowned coverage for both
  weapons and power-ups, plus a no-duplicate draw test.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` — verify/adjust the custom selection
  strategy still always offers a `weapon-level` option without duplicates.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` (and any other
  choice-path integration test) — assert the real `PlayScene` draw never
  contains a base + level-up pair for the same id.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.5 — update the hold-full-choice paragraph to
  state the base entry is suppressed once an item is owned.

## Related work

- **Weapon Leveling (AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J)** — parent design for run-scoped
  weapon levels and persistent-level semantics (AC2) this fix preserves.
- **Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list
  (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR)** — introduced `isNew`/`changeSummary`; explains why the
  base-pool entry and the level-up entry both exist today.
- **Design level curves for all power-ups (AH-0MU2QJE2007JNR6)** — the
  power-up-level counterpart governed by Q2 = Yes.
- **Design level curves for all power-ups (AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9)** — power-up
  level integration contract (persistence, stack reconciliation).
- **Power-up choice strategy (AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q)** — origin of the pluggable
  `ChoiceStrategy` / `CHOICE_POOL`.
- **Weapon level-up offers (AH-0MUPOVYZU0073OUV)** — added the `weapon-level`
  candidates that create the duplicate.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **AH-0MTGS8TWU006WTFX** – Wire shoot audio into GymWeapons._autoFire() (completed)
- **AH-0MU7JTF9W008B8HW** – Player cannot move during wave/level transition pauses (completed)
- **AH-0MUH6LEYY0054E63** – Wire the runtime auto-sequencer into the game's wave generation (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: already, appear, base, basic, behaviour (+46 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: already, appear, base, basic, behaviour (+41 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: already, appear, base, behaviour, cause (+33 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — regression in gym strategy.** `GymWeaponLeveling` relies on the
  base pool for filler options; after suppression the filler list is smaller.
  Mitigation: the number of level-up offers grows with owned items, and the
  strategy still degrades gracefully; cover with the gym parity tests.
- **Risk — "New" badge semantics.** Suppressing the base entry for owned items
  could hide a re-collect path. Assumption: the levelled offer is the intended
  re-collect/upgrade path (same permanent `equipWeapon` effect), so nothing
  gameplay-relevant is lost. Documented in the brief.
- **Risk — power-up hybrid (P9/P10).** Base-pool `powerup` and `power-up-level`
  are applied identically today, so suppression is safe; keep an eye on the
  P9/P10 timed-vs-permanent distinction in tests.
- **Assumption — scope.** Only candidate de-duplication is in scope; no change
  to level persistence, drop timing or permanent-grant semantics.
- **Scope-creep guard.** Any desire to change *temporary vs permanent level*
  semantics (the reporter's literal "timed Lvl 2 should expire to Lvl 1")
  conflicts with AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J AC2 and is **out of scope** here; raise it
  as a separate work item if wanted.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (fix direction):** "Which behaviour is intended — A) suppress the
  base-pool entry when owned and keep persistent levels; B) keep the base entry
  and drop the levelled entry; C) separate temporary vs permanent levels so
  temporary collections do not persist?"
  — **Answer (operator):** **A** — de-duplicate only; keep the existing
  persistent-level model (AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J AC2 unchanged). Source: interactive
  reply, 2026-10-05.
- **Q2 (power-up parity):** "Apply the same de-duplication to power-ups
  (P3–P10 base offers vs `power-up-level` offers)?"
  — **Answer (operator):** **Yes.** Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-05.
- **Root-cause research (no question needed):** verified in
  `src/powerups/choice.ts` (`buildChoiceCandidates`) and
  `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` (`applyMineralChoiceReward`) that the two
  offers are produced unconditionally for any owned item and are functionally
  identical; the reporter's temporary-drops hypothesis is an instance, not the
  cause. Recorded as a comment on this work item.

# Test matrix and shared fixtures for the P3/P4 effect path

## Summary
Establish the shared test fixtures/helpers and the documented case matrix from
AC8 that the P3 multi-hit and P4 ranged-pulse implementation features (F2/F3/F4)
consume. This is test-first infrastructure only: it adds no failing specs, so
every commit stays green while giving the implementation features a single,
reusable harness.

## User story
As an implementing agent, I want reusable fixtures and a documented test matrix
for the P3/P4 effect path so that each behaviour change lands with focused,
non-duplicated tests.

- AC1 — A documented test matrix (in the work-item comment or a test-runner
  comment) enumerates every case required by parent AC8: per-level P3 absorb
  counts; P3 level-0 single-hit backward compatibility; P4 field single-pulse
  and consumption; P4 permanent immediate + interval pulses with per-level
  range; reset semantics; level persistence across timeouts; choice-summary
  truthfulness; game↔gym equality.
- AC2 — Reusable fixtures/helpers exist for constructing an `EffectsRegistry`
  with a `PowerUpLevelStore` at a chosen level and for asserting a ranged
  enemy-bullet clear, without duplicating scene setup.

  failing/red specs are added by this item.
- AC4 — Test-only change: no production behaviour is modified.

- Parent AC8 trace: **AC8 — Tests.** Unit + parity tests cover: multi-hit absorb counts per P3
## Key Files
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts`

## Dependencies
None — this is the first item and unblocks F2/F3.

# P3 multi-hit shield absorption and HUD remaining-hits

**Parent:** AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB. **Type:** feature.

## Summary
Wire the levelled `shieldAbsorptions` axis into the effect path: a shield at
upgrade level L absorbs L resolved hits before popping, instead of always one.
Surface the remaining absorptions in the HUD.

## User story
As a player, when my shield is levelled it should absorb the promised number of
hits before popping — not always one — and I should see how many absorptions
remain.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC1 — `EffectsRegistry` tracks a run-scoped remaining-absorptions count
  resolved from `store.stats('P3').shieldAbsorptions`.
- AC2 — A shield active at upgrade level L absorbs exactly that many hits
  before popping; at level 0 it behaves exactly as today (single hit).
- AC3 — The shield remains a single activation whose remaining count is

# Spike: automated gameplay video capture (headless browser + scripted bot)

## Problem statement

There is currently no way to produce a gameplay video of AI_Hell without a
human recording their screen. We want to prove, end to end, that a gameplay
video can be generated **automatically** (no manual screen recording) and to
record a recommended approach together with the real costs and limits. This
is a **time-boxed spike** (~1–2 days): the deliverable is a working
proof-of-concept plus a written recommendation, not a production feature.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I want a repeatable command that boots
AI_Hell in a real rendering browser, plays a deterministic scripted segment,
and writes a playable video file, so I can generate demo/attract clips and
(potentially) regression-capture gameplay without manual recording.

## Users

- **Primary — the maintainer / release owner.** Generates demo, attract, and
  marketing clips, and wants a repeatable way to capture gameplay for
  bug reports and (later) regression evidence.
  - *As the maintainer, I can run one documented command and get a playable
    clip showing real gameplay, so I no longer have to record my screen
    manually.*
  - *As the maintainer, I can read which capture approach was proven and why
    the others were rejected, so I can decide whether to invest in a
    production capture pipeline.*
- **Secondary — future CI / QA work.** An eventual opt-in CI job could use
  the same path to capture gameplay evidence; this spike only needs to
  record the estimated cost so that decision can be made later.

## Existing state

The game is a Phaser 4 + TypeScript browser game served by Vite
(`npm run dev` / `npm run preview`). Reusable foundations already present:

- **Deterministic boot harness** — `src/test/gameHarness.ts` boots a real
  `Phaser.Game`, supports fixed-delta scene stepping and a
  `deterministicBoot` option (tracked by AH-0MUHA0MMP001DZ5C).
- **Seeded VFX RNG** — `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts` and
  `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` use `createRng` / `mulberry32`, designed for
  deterministic replays.
- **Self-contained gym scenes** — `src/scenes/gym/` isolate one mechanic
  each, and are good short-form video subjects.
- **Offline WAV audio pipeline** — `scripts/build-audio.mjs` /
  `scripts/build-audio.sh` (`npm run build-audio`) renders audio without a
  browser.

Confirmed gaps:

1. **No capture/encode path.** No Playwright/Puppeteer in `node_modules`, no
   Chromium, no `ffmpeg` on `PATH`. CI cannot render at all:
   `src/test/setup.ts` stubs the canvas with a no-op Proxy, so browser render
   verification is a manual `npm run dev` step. Real video needs a **real**
   rendering browser.
2. **No automated player.** No autoplay/attract mode or scripted input.
   Tests drive scenes directly via `scene.tick(dt)` and synthesised
   `KeyboardEvent`s, which a bot could reuse, but nothing exists.

## Candidate approaches to evaluate (prove at least one end to end)

- **A. Headless Chromium + MediaRecorder:** Playwright loads the page,
  `canvas.captureStream(60)` → `MediaRecorder` → `.webm`, optional `ffmpeg`
  → `.mp4`.
- **B. CDP screencast / per-frame capture:** Playwright CDP
  `Page.startScreencast` or `canvas.toDataURL` per frame, piped to `ffmpeg`.
- **C. In-engine snapshot loop:** dev-only mode using
  `Phaser game.renderer.snapshot()` on a fixed tick, frames written and
  encoded externally (audio captured separately).
- **D. Deterministic replay:** drive `src/test/gameHarness.ts` with a
  recorded/seeded input sequence, render headless, encode (best
  reproducibility; needs bot + headless renderer).

For whichever path is chosen, the spike must also handle a **minimal
automated player** (scripted input or a simple heuristic bot) sufficient to
produce a non-trivial clip.

## Known constraints

- **Audio:** browsers block `AudioContext` before a user gesture; capture via
  `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode`, or reuse the offline WAV pipeline
  (`scripts/build-audio.mjs`).
- **Determinism:** only VFX RNG is seeded; wave/spawn/timing randomness still
  uses wall-clock and `Math.random()`, so runs are not currently
  reproducible without further seeding. Identified unseeded sources include
  `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`, `src/entities/Swarm.ts`, `src/entities/Boss.ts`,
  `src/entities/Scout.ts`, `src/entities/Mineral.ts` and
  `src/entities/Asteroid.ts`.
- **CI cost:** a headless browser + encoder is a heavy dependency — recommend
  running as an opt-in local/CI job, not part of `npm test`.
- **Opt-in only:** all additions must sit behind a dev-only/opt-in path so
  the shipped game and the vitest suite are unaffected. Do **not** edit
  `.pi/`, `skill/`, or `command/` infrastructure.

## Desired change

1. Prove the capture path end to end with a single documented command
   (e.g. `npm run capture` or equivalent) that boots the game in a real
   rendering browser, plays a scripted segment automatically, and writes a
   playable video locally.
2. Add a minimal automated player (scripted sequence or simple heuristic bot)
   that drives a deterministic, non-trivial gameplay segment.
3. Write down the recommended approach (tooling + versions, exact commands,
   output format) and at least two rejected alternatives with reasons.
4. Document the known limits: headless WebGL reliability, audio capture
   status (captured or explicitly deferred), determinism gaps, and estimated
   CI cost (browser download + encode time).

Prefer approach A for the fastest end-to-end proof unless it fails on
headless WebGL. Time-box the investigation to roughly 1–2 days.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — add an opt-in `capture` script and dev-only capture
  dependencies; must not affect `npm test` / `npm run build`.
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — **new**. Orchestration: launch headless
  Chromium, load dev/preview server, run the bot, capture frames/stream,
  encode to a video file.
- `scripts/capture-bot.mjs` or `src/capture/` — **new**. Deterministic
  scripted input / heuristic bot driving keyboard events into the page.
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — reuse `deterministicBoot` / fixed-delta
  stepping; possibly expose a replay/driver hook.
- `src/main.ts` / `src/core/boot.ts` — optional dev-only capture flag /
  attract-mode entry (gated, no shipped-bundle impact).
- `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`, `src/vfx/playerDeathJuice.ts` — seeded RNG
  to align with deterministic replay.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts`, `src/entities/*.ts` — unseeded `Math.random()`
  sources identified as determinism gaps.
- `scripts/build-audio.mjs` — reuse the offline WAV pipeline for optional
  audio.
- `docs/` — new capture/recommendation doc, e.g.
  `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (plus README pointer if appropriate).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single documented command (e.g. `npm run capture` or equivalent) boots
   AI_Hell in a real rendering browser, plays a scripted segment
   automatically, and writes a playable video file locally.
2. The produced video is verifiably non-trivial: it shows actual
   gameplay/VFX (not a black or static frame), with duration and resolution
   recorded.
3. The automated player is described and committed: how it generates input
   (scripted sequence or bot) and which segment/scene it drives.
4. The recommended approach is written down (in the work item and/or
   `docs/`) covering: chosen tooling and versions, exact commands, output
   format, and at least the two rejected alternatives with reasons.
5. Known limits are documented: headless WebGL reliability, audio capture
   status (captured or explicitly deferred), and current determinism gaps
   (unseeded wave/spawn randomness).
6. The change is additive/opt-in: `npm test` and `npm run build` still pass
   unchanged; no impact on the shipped bundle unless explicitly gated behind
   a dev-only flag.
7. Estimated CI cost (browser download + encode time) is recorded so the
   maintainer can decide whether to run it in CI.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** approach A (headless Chromium + MediaRecorder) is tried
  first; the operator may redirect the preferred approach.
- **Risk — headless WebGL:** `Phaser.AUTO` may fall back to canvas or fail to
  render in headless Chromium; mitigation is approach C (`renderer.snapshot()`)
  or forcing the `WEBGL`/`CANVAS` renderer explicitly.
- **Risk — determinism:** runs are not reproducible until the unseeded
  wave/spawn RNG is addressed; the clip is still valuable without full
  determinism, so this is documented rather than solved in this spike.
- **Risk — heavy dependency:** browser + encoder download/encode time may be
  large; mitigation is opt-in tooling excluded from `npm test`/`npm run build`.
- **Risk — scope creep (explicit):** productionising capture, seeding all RNG,
  wiring CI, or shipping an attract mode are **out of scope**; record any such
  follow-up as a linked work item rather than expanding this spike.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUHA0MMP001DZ5C** — introduced the deterministic boot harness
  (`deterministicBoot`); the fixed-delta stepping this spike can reuse.
- **AH-0MUJK70PU003VLIB** — documents the deterministic harness boot / tick
  convention.
- **AH-0MUJK6XHY004GPJT** — removed the wave-clear / transition-start
  nondeterminism; precedent for determinism fixes.
- **AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD** — deterministic WAV build pipeline; the offline
  audio option for captured video.
- **AH-0MUGCI3F80030J31** / **AH-0MUGCP15V0008339** — seeded-RNG determinism
  for `AsteroidSpawner` / `PlayScene` spawner; precedent for seeding the
  remaining wave/spawn randomness.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN** – Enemy Design tooling (completed)
- **AH-0MTCO9KKY007GOND** – [test-failure] <suite exited 1>: npm --silent test — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MUTV7632000ZWCB** – Victory and defeat end-of-run fanfare (audio + visual juice) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, actual, additive, also, approach (+203 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: actual, additive, also, approach, approaches (+181 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: actual, also, audio, automatically, best (+159 more)

> Note: the automated matches above are low-signal keyword co-occurrences
> (generic docs terms); the curated "Related work" list above is the
> authoritative set.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (intake agent, to self / repo search): Is the seed context sufficient
  to draft a clear brief without an interview round?**
  — **Answer:** Yes. The operator's seed already supplies a clear goal, user
  story, candidate approaches, constraints, and 7 measurable acceptance
  criteria; the repo search confirmed the stated existing foundations and
  gaps. No clarifying questions were required. Source: seed description +
  repo inspection (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`, `src/test/setup.ts`,
  `src/vfx/`, `src/waves/`, `package.json`).
- **Q (intake agent): Which capture approach should the spike commit to up
  front?**
  — **Answer (assumption, recorded):** The spike evaluates the candidates and
  proves at least one end to end; approach A (headless Chromium +
  MediaRecorder) is the preferred first attempt for the fastest proof, with
  B/C/D as fallbacks. Source: seed description. This is an assumption, not a
  producer decision — the operator may redirect the preferred approach.
- **Q (intake agent): Should the captured clip include audio?**
  — **OPEN QUESTION (deferred to the spike):** Audio capture is explicitly
  listed as a constraint to investigate; the spike may capture via
  `MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode` or explicitly defer audio and reuse the
  offline WAV pipeline. Source: seed description.
data.title: Spike: automated gameplay video capture (headless browser + scripted bot)

discovered-from:AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK

## Problem statement
`npm run capture` produces **no console output for ~20 s** (browser/ Vite startup + 2 s warm-up + 15 s recording + decode), so a normal run looks like a hang. A missing `playwright` devDependency (or its browser) also fails with a raw `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` / Playwright stack instead of an actionable setup step.

**User story:** As the maintainer, I want live progress and an ETA while a capture runs, and a clear preflight error when the capture dependencies are missing, so I can tell a running capture from a hung one and know how to fix setup.

## Desired change
1. Emit startup milestones (headless Chromium launch, game load, PlayScene start, recording start, encoding/probe).
2. During the recording loop, print a periodic (>= every ~2 s) progress line with elapsed / total and an ETA (e.g. a single overwriting line).
3. Preflight the `playwright` import and browser availability; on failure print `Run: npm install && npm run capture:install` and exit non-zero — no raw stack trace.
4. Keep the existing final report on stdout and keep `--json` machine-readable (progress on stderr so stdout stays parseable).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Capture prints distinct startup milestones (browser launch, game load, scene start, recording) as they happen.
2. While recording, progress output shows elapsed/total and a time-to-completion estimate at least every ~2 s.
3. A missing `playwright` package or browser produces a short actionable message naming `npm install && npm run capture:install` and exits non-zero (no `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` stack).
4. Progress goes to stderr; the final human report keeps going to stdout and `--json` remains valid JSON on stdout.
5. Pure formatting/ETA helper(s) are unit-tested; the full project test suite passes.
6. Docs/README updated to mention the progress output and preflight.
