# Full-run capture wait, tail and cap

## Summary

Change the **default** demo capture from a fixed-duration clip to a **complete
run**: wait for the end-of-run signal, keep recording a configurable tail
(default `5000` ms), enforce a safety cap, and report the outcome
(parent AH-0MUX2K8U7000GFNU, AC2/AC3).

**User story:** As the maintainer, I run `npm run capture` once and get a video
of a complete run from Play Game/Watch Demo to 5 s past victory or defeat; if
the run never signals, the tool stops at `--max-duration` and tells me the clip
is incomplete instead of pretending it is a full run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** The default (demo) path installs the run-end listener **before the
  game boots** (`page.addInitScript`) and also reads `window.__aiHellRunState`
  as a race fallback, so an early end is not missed.
- **AC2:** `npm run capture` records a complete run from the start of play to
  game over, then continues for `--tail <ms>` (default `5000`) and stops,
  reporting the detected outcome and run length.
- **AC3:** A configurable `--max-duration` cap bounds the recording. When the
  cap is hit with no signal, the tool reports it explicitly and **exits
  non-zero** — a capped clip is never presented as a complete run.
- **AC4:** `--duration` and `--scripted` retain the existing fixed-length
  behaviour; only the default demo path becomes full-run.
- **AC5:** Progress/heartbeat works across an unbounded (capped) recording and
  reports elapsed vs cap.
- **AC6:** Unit tests cover arg parsing for `--tail`/`--max-duration`, the
  listener-install plan, and the pure wait/stop loop; the stubbed integration
  assertion lives in the verification child.
- **AC7:** `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace the demo fixed-duration `while` loop with a wait loop driven by the
  pure helpers: poll the signal/flag and the clock, stop at
  `signalTime + tail` or the cap.
- Parse `--tail` / `--max-duration`; keep defaults single-source.
- Update the help text and `--json` payload with outcome/complete/cap fields.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — wait/tail/cap loop, listener install, reporting
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.d.mts` — options/result types
- `scripts/capture-progress.mjs` — heartbeat for an unbounded recording
- `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts` — arg/loop tests
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — the signal emitter (dependency)

## Dependencies

Depends on **Run-end signal, tail and dwell helpers** and **Emit dev-gated
end-of-run signal**.

## Deliverables

Full-run default capture with tail, cap, and explicit cap-hit failure.

## Summary
The game's gameplay RNG (wave/spawn/timing) currently draws from wall-clock and Math.random(), so two runs of the same scenario differ. Give every run a **seed** that drives all gameplay randomness, expose/persist it, and thread it through the code the bot and telemetry need.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A per-run seed is generated (or supplied via scene-start data / config) and stored on `GameState`; `PlayScene` exposes it (e.g. `getRunSeed()`).
- AC2: All gameplay RNG sources (WaveManager, Swarm, Boss, Scout, Mineral, Asteroid timing) derive from a seeded RNG, not Math.random()/wall clock. Enumerate the sources and convert each.
- AC3: Same seed + same inputs reproduces the same run (deterministic test over N ticks; two runs agree).
- AC4: The seed is available to the bot snapshot/telemetry layer and recorded with every run.
- AC5: Existing tests pass; unseeded startup still works (a fresh random seed per run).

## Notes
Enables replay, same-seed bot-vs-human evaluation and telemetry correlation. Previously deferred as out of scope in AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ.
data.title: Deterministic run seeding and seed plumbing

data.description:
## Summary
Build the **telemetry framework**: a versioned, consent-gated, pluggable pipeline that is a strict no-op unless enabled. It must work identically in dev and production and be safe/privacy-preserving.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A `TelemetryRecorder` interface with versioned record schemas (run header with seed/schema version/build; per-tick state+input; discrete events).
- AC2: Pluggable sinks behind one interface: a local JSONL dev sink and a remote/production sink stub; a no-op sink used when disabled.
- AC3: **Disabled by default**; explicitly enabled via config/env. A consent flag gates production recording.
- AC4: Bounded overhead/backpressure (ring buffer + batched flush) so recording never stalls gameplay; a documented sampling option.
- AC5: No PII in the schema; secrets/tokens excluded; documented data policy.
- AC6: Unit tests: no-op sink records nothing; JSONL sink round-trips; batching/flush; schema version present.
- AC7: Docs: schema reference + how to enable/disable.
data.title: Telemetry framework: versioned schema, pluggable sinks, consent flag

## Summary
Replace the per-frame priority ladder with a **bot framework**: a world model, a registry of goals/behaviours, a committed policy and a content configuration seam. This is the maintainable core that later content and styles plug into.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A `BotBrain`/policy interface that maps a `BotSnapshot` (+ world model + memory) to an input, with an explicit **commitment** mechanism (a selected goal is held until achieved, invalidated, or outranked by a margin for a minimum time).
- AC2: A **goal/behaviour registry**: goals and behaviours register by id; adding one does not require editing the core switch/if-chain.
- AC3: A world-model/predictor layer (positions/velocities, incoming-fire prediction) separated from decision policy, so prediction is testable in isolation.
- AC4: The existing pure `decideBotInput` is preserved behind an adapter (so current tests/gyms keep working) or cleanly superseded with documented parity tests.
- AC5: The framework is deterministic and pure over an injected `dt`/clock; no wall-clock dependence.
- AC6: Unit tests: registry, commitment/hysteresis, deterministic replay of a decision sequence.
- AC7: Docs: framework overview + how goals/behaviours are structured.
data.title: Bot framework core: world model, goal/behaviour registry, committed policy

# Repo-wide power-up ID literal guard (test-first)

## Summary
Add an automated guard test that fails while any legacy `'P3'`-`'P10'` power-up
literal remains under `src/`, so the name-based rename (parent
AH-0MUX6S20F002GHPF) cannot be silently left half-done.

## User story
As a maintainer, I want a single automated guard that fails with the exact
`file:line` of any surviving legacy power-up ID, so I can trust that AC1 of the
parent is complete without a manual grep.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A new test module `src/powerups/powerUpIdNaming.test.ts` scans all
   `src/**/*.ts` (source and tests) and fails, listing `file:line`, when a
   quoted power-up literal matching `'P3'`, `'P4'`, `'P5'`, `'P6'`, `'P7'`,
   `'P8'`, `'P9'` or `'P10'` is found.
2. The guard carries an explicit, documented allow-list (leaving `P1`/`P2`
   weapon IDs resolved in `src/utils/weapons.ts` untouched) and fails if an
   allow-listed entry no longer matches, preventing a stale allow-list from
   hiding a regression.

   is wired into the standard `vitest run` suite (no opt-in flag needed).

## Minimal implementation
- Add `src/powerups/powerUpIdNaming.test.ts` using `node:fs` to walk `src/`.
- Regex: `['"](P3|P4|P5|P6|P7|P8|P9|P10)['"]`; collect and assert the set is
  empty, reporting offenders in the failure message.
- Keep the allow-list minimal and data-driven; assert every entry is still
  matched (stale-entry check).

## Dependencies
None — this is the first (test-first) item.

- Red-before / green-after evidence recorded on the parent.

# Migrate persisted powerUpWeights to name keys

## Summary
Bump `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` and translate a stored legacy P-keyed
`powerUpWeights` table to the new name keys in `loadRules()`, so customised
drop weights survive the rename (localStorage key `ai-hell-game-rules`).

## User story
As a player with tuned spawn weights, I want my customised drop weights to
survive the upgrade so the rename does not silently reset my configuration.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped from `3` to `4`.
2. `loadRules()` migrates a stored legacy `powerUpWeights` table from the
   `P3`-`P10` keys to the equivalent name keys; unknown or non-numeric keys are
   still ignored; partial tables are still merged over defaults; an
   already-name-keyed config is unchanged.
3. A regression test proves a version-3 config with a customised P-keyed
   weight (for example `P8: 9`) loads under the equivalent name key
   (`extra_life: 9`) with every other rule preserved, and that a version-4
   name-keyed config round-trips unchanged.
4. `saveRules()` persists name-keyed weights with `version: 4`; the existing
   version-1/2 mineral-hold and re-drop migrations are unchanged.

### Parent AC coverage (AH-0MUX6S20F002GHPF)

- **Persisted rules migrate.** `RULES_SCHEMA_VERSION` is bumped and `loadRules()` migrates a stored legacy `powerUpWeights` table from the `P3`–`P10` keys to the new name keys, so customised drop weights survive the upgrade. A regression test proves a version-3 config with customised P-keyed weights loads under the equivalent name keys.

## Minimal implementation
- Add a `LEGACY_POWER_UP_ID_BY_CODE` map (`P3` -> `shield`, ... `P10` ->

- Extend `mergeWeights(stored)` (or add a migration pass keyed on

# Intake Brief — Enhance Central AI boss encounter

**Work item:** Enhance Central AI boss encounter: 200 HP, more minions, figure-8 movement, top-screen health bar, hit feedback (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X)

## Problem statement

The Central AI boss encounter is currently a static, 400-hit grind: the boss does not move, the health bar is drawn relative to the boss container (so it is visibly displaced rather than at the top of the screen), and individual hits give no feedback beyond a bullet disappearing. Players cannot read their progress and the fight lacks the mobility and impact expected of a climactic boss. This work item reduces the boss's total health to **200**, reinforces the fight with **more minions**, gives the boss **figure-of-8 movement**, fixes the **health bar to the top of the screen**, and makes **every hit obvious through SFX and VFX**.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** fights the boss after clearing Level 5 and wants a readable, impactful, mobile encounter.
  - *As a player, I want to see the boss's health decrease with every hit so I know my shots are registering.*
  - *As a player, I want the fight to feel dynamic and dangerous, with the boss moving and more enemies on screen.*
  - *As a player, I want clear audio/visual feedback on each hit so the encounter feels responsive.*
- **Developer/maintainer (secondary):** wants the change implemented once in the shared core so the game and boss gyms stay in parity.
  - *As a developer, I want the boss behaviour to live in the shared core so `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` cannot diverge.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Boss total health is 200.** The boss spawns with 200 total hits across the existing **4 phases (50 hits per phase)**. The 4-phase structure, phase transitions, and score/minion rewards gated on *depleting* hits are preserved. Verified by unit tests: hit 49 stays in phase 1, hit 50 advances to phase 2, and hit 200 destroys the boss.
2. **More minions are spawned with the boss.** Phase 1 spawns **12 scouts** (6 per side), phase 2 spawns **12 divers** (6 per side), phase 3 remains **0** (the pulse is the threat), and phase 4 spawns **15 swarm**. Verified by `BossMinions` unit tests asserting the per-phase counts via `minionCountForPhase`.
3. **The boss moves in a figure-of-8 pattern.** The boss traces a lemniscate around its spawn anchor (≈120 px horizontal, ≈60 px vertical amplitude, ≈8 s per full cycle), staying within the playfield. Movement is implemented once in the shared boss/combat core and is identical in `PlayScene` and every boss gym. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live position, and the health bar does not move with it. Verified by tests asserting the traced position and bounded amplitude.
4. **The health bar is fixed at the top of the screen and decreases per hit.** The bar is camera-fixed, horizontally centred at the top of the playfield, always visible during the encounter, and **not** offset or moved by the boss's figure-8 motion. Its fill shrinks proportionally on every hit (200 → 0) with the four phase-segment dividers retained. Verified by tests asserting the bar's screen position is independent of the boss position and that `getHpFraction()` decreases after hits.
5. **Hits on the boss are obvious with both SFX and VFX.** Every hit on the boss plays a dedicated boss-hit SFX cue and spawns an obvious impact VFX (flash/burst) at the hit point; phase transitions retain their existing distinct cue and visual. Game and gym use the same shared feedback path. Verified by the cue-manifest contract test (new cue registered) and VFX tests (an impact effect is registered per hit).
6. **Test coverage.** New/updated tests cover the health model, minion counts, figure-8 motion, health-bar placement, and hit feedback across `Boss.test.ts`, `BossMinions.test.ts`, `GymBoss.test.ts`, `PlayScene.test.ts`, and the audio cue contract.
7. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the Game Design Document (§4.3), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§5.1 parity), and the audio cue mapping/manifest.
8. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (mandatory):** gameplay behaviour must live in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/entities/`) and be consumed by both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss`; no divergent copies. The `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs assertion must still pass.
- **Preserve the 4-phase model:** do not change the phase attack patterns, telegraphs, or reward gating; only retune totals/counts and add movement/feedback.
- **Health bar model:** keep the existing proportional `getHpFraction()` fill and the four phase-segment dividers.
- **Audio pipeline:** a new SFX cue must be registered in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` and `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` (the contract test enforces completeness).
- **No new dependencies.**
- Stay within the existing visual/neon style and UK-English documentation conventions.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Boss.ts`: 4 phases × `BOSS_HIT_POINTS_PER_PHASE = 100` = **400 total hits**; `applyFormationPosition()` is a static `setPosition(baseX, baseY)`; `healthBarGraphics` is added as a **child of the boss container** but drawn with screen coordinates (so it renders offset by the boss position); `takeDamage()` only plays the phase-transition cue on a depleting hit; no per-hit feedback.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts`: phase 1 = 8 scouts (4+4), phase 2 = 8 divers (4+4), phase 3 = 0, phase 4 = 10 swarm.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_damageBoss()`: applies damage and awards score/summons minions on phase depletion; no hit SFX/VFX.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` `damageBoss()`: gym equivalent, mirrors the game's gating.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` `_advanceBoss()`: shared per-frame boss advance consumed by both the game and the gym (the correct place for shared movement/feedback).
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts`: reusable `spawnBulletImpact()` flash already used for non-lethal hits on multi-hit enemies (Harvester) but **not** wired to the boss.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` + `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` + `src/audio/cueManifest.ts`: no boss-hit cue exists.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.3 documents the 400-hit model and static boss.

## Desired change

1. Retune boss health to a **200-hit total** (4 phases × 50) and update the constants/comments/tests.
2. Increase minion counts to **P1 = 12, P2 = 12, P3 = 0, P4 = 15**.
3. Add **figure-8 (lemniscate) movement** around the spawn anchor in the shared boss core, with parameters ≈120 px / ≈60 px / ≈8 s, bounded to the playfield.
4. **Re-parent the health bar** out of the boss container so it is camera-fixed at the top-centre of the screen, always visible, and unaffected by boss movement; keep the proportional fill and phase dividers.
5. Add a **dedicated boss-hit SFX cue** and an **obvious hit VFX** (impact flash/burst at the hit point) applied on every hit through a shared path used by both the game and the gym; keep the existing phase-transition feedback.
6. Update tests and documentation (GDD, enemy design/parity doc, audio mapping).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — health constants (50/phase, 200 total), figure-8 movement, health-bar re-parenting/positioning, per-hit feedback hook.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts` — increased per-phase minion counts.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — shared boss movement/feedback seam for parity.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_damageBoss()` hit-feedback wiring; health-bar layering.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — `damageBoss()` hit-feedback wiring (parity).
- `src/audio/effects.ts`, `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` — new boss-hit cue and mapping.
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` — reusable/extended impact flash for boss hits.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts`, `src/waves/BossMinions.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUUJEB1D000GPX0** – PlayScene/GymBoss reward gating on phase depletion (completed) — established the `phaseAdvanced`-gated score/minion behaviour this work preserves.
- **AH-0MUUJCL8J00632T7** – Boss.ts per-phase HP model, return contract, health-bar fill (completed) — the `getHpFraction()` proportional fill this work keeps.
- **AH-0MUTV3J7T006MZ4K** – Increase Central AI boss hits-per-phase 10x (completed) — prior health tuning precedent.
- **AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE** – Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene (completed) — gym that must stay in parity.
- **AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ** – Integrate boss encounter into PlayScene (completed) — boss spawn wiring and minion sums.
- **AH-0MUD9R3ZC0006M4I** – Extract collision core and host bullet-vs-bullet impact feedback (completed) — shared impact-feedback precedent.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MUUJEB1D000GPX0** – PlayScene/GymBoss reward gating on phase depletion (completed)
- **AH-0MU3X86GT001YM5D** – Identify enemy refactor opportunities (completed)
- **AH-0MUUJFOTM009ORQM** – GDD and code comment documentation updates (AC7) (completed)

Repository file matches: `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (confirmed):** "200 health" means 200 total hits across 4 phases (50 each), not 200 per phase.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** minion increase ≈50% in phases 1, 2 and 4; phase 3 stays minion-free.
- **Assumption (confirmed):** figure-8 defaults 120 px / 60 px / ~8 s; boss-only motion; top-centre screen-fixed health bar; new per-hit SFX + impact-flash VFX.
- **Risk:** figure-8 motion could push the boss off-screen or desync aimed shots/minions — mitigate with bounded amplitude and using the boss's live position for aiming/collision.
- **Risk:** health-bar re-parenting may break tests that assume the bar is a container child — update those tests and add explicit screen-position assertions.
- **Risk:** the new SFX may need a ToneForge recipe/baked asset; if a new recipe is required the audio build pipeline must render it (or reuse an existing recipe) and the manifest must stay complete so the contract test passes.
- **Risk:** gameplay change requires parity across `PlayScene` and all boss gyms — implement in shared core only; verify with the equivalence/parity tests.
- **Scope-creep:** further boss rebalancing (attack patterns, telegraph timings, additional phases) is out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: What does "reduce the health to 200" mean?** Options: (a) 200 total hits across 4 phases (50 each); (b) 200 per phase (800 total); (c) other. **Recommended:** (a) — preserves the 4-phase model.
  - **Answer (operator):** "(a)". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q2: How much should the minion count increase, and in which phases?** Options: (a) ~50% more in phases 1, 2 and 4 (P1 12, P2 12, P3 0, P4 15); (b) roughly double all; (c) add minions to phase 3; (d) other. **Recommended:** (a).
  - **Answer (operator):** "(a)". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.
- **Q3: Are the implementation defaults acceptable?** (figure-8: 120 px / 60 px / ~8 s, boss-only; hit feedback: new hit SFX + impact flash on every hit, keeping phase-transition feedback; health bar: screen-fixed top-centre). **Recommended:** accept.
  - **Answer (operator):** "yes". Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-07.

# Add 10% weighting to owned upgrades in hold-full choice

## Problem statement

When the hold fills and the player is offered a choice of upgrades, owned upgrades (weapon-level / power-up-level options) should appear 10% more likely than they currently do. Currently all candidates are selected uniformly at random; owned upgrades should receive a 1.1× weight multiplier.

## Users

- **Player (progression):** "As a player, when offered a hold-full choice I want a reasonable chance of upgrading an upgradeable weapon or power-up I already own, so my build keeps improving rather than forcing me to chase new items."
- **Designer:** "As a designer, I want owned upgrades to appear 10% more often so progression feels steady across runs."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — 10% weighting.** Owned level-up offers (both `weapon-level` and `power-up-level`) have a 1.1× weight multiplier applied during candidate selection. Unowned (base-pool) items retain 1.0× weight.
- **AC2 — Single source of truth.** The weighting logic lives in the strategy layer (`createRandomChoiceStrategy`), not in `buildChoiceCandidates`; no duplicate weighting code in scenes or gyms.
- **AC3 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every gym that opens the hold-full choice, because they share `MineralChoiceScene` and `powerups/choice`.
- **AC4 — Configurable weight.** The 1.1× multiplier is a named constant (e.g. `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT = 1.1`) so it can be tuned later without hunting for magic numbers.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests verify: (a) owned-level candidates receive 1.1× weight; (b) weighted random selection produces the expected distribution (10,000 trials, ±3% tolerance, owned items appear ~10% more often than unowned items relative to pool size); (c) gym↔game parity tests pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour must live once and be consumed by both the game and every gym.
- **Backward compatible:** no breaking changes to the `ChoiceStrategy` interface or existing `ChoiceOption` consumers.
- **No gameplay logic changes beyond weighting:** the candidate list itself is unchanged — only the selection probabilities shift.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — add weighting logic in `createRandomChoiceStrategy`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — no changes expected (they already pass context).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — new tests for weighted selection (10k trials, ±3%).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — parity tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed).
- **AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J** — Weapon leveling (completed).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship'\''s hold (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Statistical testing (low):** proving 10% bias requires many trials; tests use 10,000 draws with ±3% tolerance band.
- **Scope creep (low):** adding per-weight tunability (player-facing weight editor) could expand scope. Mitigation: this item implements a single constant only; per-weight tuning is a separate chore if needed.
- **Assumption:** "10% more likely" means a 1.1× multiplicative weight, not an additive 10 percentage points.
- **Assumption:** "owned upgrade" means `weapon-level` and `power-up-level` kind options in the candidate list.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope of owned upgrades?** (A: both weapon-level and power-up-level; B: only weapon-level; C: both with different weights.) — Answer (Producer): A — both weapon-level and power-up-level.
- **Q2 — Where does weighting logic live?** (A: in `buildChoiceCandidates` with tagged weights; B: in `createRandomChoiceStrategy` strategy layer.) — Answer (Producer): B — in the strategy layer.
- **Q3 — Test tolerance for statistical validation?** (A: 10,000 trials, ±3%; B: 50,000 trials, ±1%; C: 5,000 trials, ±5%.) — Answer (Producer): A — 10,000 trials, ±3%.

# Bot still controls the player after Watch Demo then Play Game

## Problem statement

After the player selects **Watch Demo** on the main menu, every subsequent
**Play Game** start can inherit the demo's scene data, so the bot keeps
driving the ship instead of the keyboard. This is a critical, player-visible
control bug: the player cannot actually play a normal run until the page is
reloaded.

## Users

- **Player** — selects Watch Demo, then Play Game, and expects full keyboard
  control in the new run.
  - *As a player, after watching the demo I want Play Game to hand me full
    keyboard control so I can play a normal run.*
  - *As a player, taking over the demo with a key and later starting a fresh
    game must not leave the bot steering my ship.*

## Root cause (verified against the pinned Phaser source)

Phaser's `Systems.start(data)` only assigns `settings.data` when `data` is
truthy:

```js
// node_modules/phaser/src/scene/Systems.js
start: function (data) {
    if (data) { settings.data = data; }
    ...
}
```

`SceneManager.start(key, data)` forwards `data` as-is, and
`SceneManager` invokes `scene.init.call(scene, settings.data)`. Because this
scene instance is reused:

1. **Watch Demo** → `MenuScene.startDemo()` calls
   `this.scene.start('PlayScene', { demo: true })` → `settings.data` becomes
   `{ demo: true }` and `PlayScene.init()` sets `demoMode = true`.
2. The demo ends (or the player takes over with a key). PlayScene shuts down
   (its `settings.data` is **not** cleared).
3. **Play Game** → `this.scene.start('PlayScene')` passes **no data**, so
   `Systems.start(undefined)` leaves the stale `{ demo: true }` in place;
   `PlayScene.init()` reads it again and re-enables demo mode, and
   `getBotInput()` therefore returns the bot decision instead of `null`.

Both normal Play Game entry points are affected (pointer handler and the
`FocusManager` keyboard activation) because both omit the data argument.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts:127` and `:267` start `PlayScene` with no data;
  `:316` (`startDemo`) starts it with `{ demo: true }`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:474` `init(data)` sets
  `this.demoMode = data?.demo === true`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts:1405` `getBotInput()` returns the governed bot
  input only while `demoMode` is true.
- Existing tests only assert normal start is non-demo on a **fresh boot**
  (`PlayScene.test.ts` "AC6 — demo mode is false when started normally"), so
  the stale-data path is untested.

## Desired change

A normal Play Game start (and any non-demo restart) must always run with the
bot disabled, regardless of whether a demo ran earlier in the same session.
The fix must be explicit rather than relying on Phaser's data-clearing
behaviour, so a future scene start that omits data cannot silently re-enter
demo mode.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — No bot after demo then Play Game.** With the game booted, start
  the demo (`MenuScene.startDemo()`), let the demo scene shut down (or take
  over), then start a normal game via the Play Game path and assert
  `PlayScene.isDemoMode() === false` and `getBotInput() === null`; the ship
  responds to keyboard input, not the bot.
- [ ] **AC2 — Explicit data on every normal start.** Both normal Play Game
  entry points in `MenuScene` pass an explicit non-demo payload
  (e.g. `{ demo: false }`), and a regression test proves a normal start after
  a demo does not inherit `{ demo: true }` from Phaser's reused
  `settings.data`.
- [ ] **AC3 — PlayScene is fail-safe.** `PlayScene.init()` treats absent,
  `undefined`, or non-`true` data as non-demo, and the scene-start contract is
  documented in the `init()`/`startDemo()` comments so a future caller cannot
  omit the flag and accidentally re-enter demo mode.
- [ ] **AC4 — Gym↔game parity preserved.** The fix touches only the
  game/gym-shared demo-input seam; the shared
  `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity
  docs assertion still pass, and no gym gains divergent demo handling.
- [ ] **AC5 — Automated regression test.** At least one automated test
  reproduces the exact sequence (Watch Demo → return to menu/take-over →
  normal Play Game) and fails on the pre-fix code; it lives at the
  MenuScene↔PlayScene integration boundary.
- [ ] **AC6 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the gym↔game parity convention in `AGENTS.md`: share demo-input
  behaviour via `src/scenes/core/`; no divergent copies.
- Do not change demo/attract behaviour itself (start, take-over, non-scoring
  end-of-run, idle timer) — only the data-handling that leaks demo mode into
  normal play.
- Keep the fix minimal and local to the scene-start data path.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** reproduction requires only the same page session (Phaser
  reuses the scene instance); no persistence is involved.
- **Risk:** other `scene.start('PlayScene')` call sites (present or future)
  could re-introduce the leak — mitigated by AC2 (explicit payloads) and AC3
  (fail-safe `init`) plus the regression test.
- **Risk:** changing the normal-start payload could affect tests that assert
  `init()` receives no data — covered by running the full suite (AC7).
- **Scope creep:** unrelated demo-mode polish (reaction time, capture tooling)
  is out of scope; record any such finds as separate linked work items.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — pass explicit `{ demo: false }` on both normal
  Play Game starts (pointer handler + `FocusManager` activation).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — harden `init()` against absent/stale data and
  document the start-data contract.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` — assert the normal Play Game payload.
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — end-to-end regression test for
  Watch Demo → Play Game.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — restart-after-demo regression coverage.
- `docs/` demo/attract documentation — note the explicit start-data contract.

## Related work

See the automated report below, plus the parent demo-mode work items:
Attract/demo entry point in MenuScene (AH-0MUX4966Z0009P9Q), Demo mode engine:
input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene (AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY), Demo-mode
integration and regression verification (AH-0MUX496TY005FF3P), and Demo bot:
human-like input limits (AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was not interview-driven: the operator supplied the reproduction,
the root cause was verified against the pinned Phaser source, and the operator
set the priority (`critical`). No open questions remain.

- Q: "Where exactly does the demo leak into a normal run?" — Answer
  (agent, verified): Phaser's `Systems.start(data)` only writes
  `settings.data` for truthy data, so a no-argument
  `scene.start('PlayScene')` after `{ demo: true }` reuses the stale payload.
  Source: `node_modules/phaser/src/scene/Systems.js:740-744`,
  `SceneManager.js:1255-1262`, `MenuScene.ts:127,267,316`,
  `PlayScene.ts:474,1405`.
- Assumption: the fix should be explicit at the call sites *and* fail-safe in
  `PlayScene.init()` (recorded under Acceptance Criteria AC2/AC3).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** – Feature: Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration tests (completed)
- **AH-0MUITRWLO001Y4Y5** – End-to-end acceptance tests for sequenced wave generation (completed)
- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** – Spike: automated gameplay video capture (headless browser + scripted bot) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: bot, bug, call, calls, cause (+49 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: bot, call, calls, cause, controls (+44 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: bot, call, calls, cause, controls (+38 more)

# Demo mode: ESC returns to the main menu; only movement keys take over

*In attract/demo mode, only ESC and the movement keys (W/A/S/D or arrows) should affect the run: ESC returns to the main menu, a movement key hands control to the player in place, and every other key and the pointer are ignored.*

## Problem statement

In attract/demo mode, **any** keyboard key or pointer press currently hands control to the player in place (`setDemoMode(false)`). This is far too sensitive for an unattended attract loop: an accidental keypress or a stray click silently drops the demo into human control instead of keeping the bot playing. The operator wants only deliberate, gameplay-relevant input to affect the demo — **ESC** to leave to the main menu, and the **movement keys** (W/A/S/D or the arrow keys) to take over as normal play. All other input must be ignored.

## Users

- **As an arcade operator running the attract loop**, I want the demo to keep playing unattended so that stray keypresses or mouse activity do not silently drop it into human control.
- **As a player who has just watched the demo**, I want to press a movement key (W/A/S/D or an arrow key) to take over and keep playing the current run.
- **As a player or operator who wants to leave the demo**, I want to press ESC to return cleanly to the main menu.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I leave the cabinet unattended in demo mode; someone bumps a random key/property the mouse, and the demo keeps playing as if nothing happened.
- As a player, the demo is running and I press **W** or the **up arrow** — I am now in control of the ship mid-run, exactly as before.
- As a player, the demo is running and I press **ESC** — I land back on the main menu.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — ESC returns to the main menu.** While `PlayScene` is in demo mode, pressing **ESC** returns directly to `MenuScene`. It must **not** take over the run and must **not** open the pause menu. ESC in non-demo play continues to toggle the pause menu, unchanged.
2. **AC2 — Movement keys take over.** While in demo mode, pressing a **movement key** — W/A/S/D (using the player's configured `moveUp`/`moveDown`/`moveLeft`/`moveRight` bindings) or an **arrow key** — calls `setDemoMode(false)` in place; the run continues and the keyboard then drives the ship. Rebinding movement keys is honoured.
3. **AC3 — All other input is ignored.** While in demo mode, any other keyboard key (e.g. Space, Enter, Tab, letters/numbers, function keys) is ignored and the demo keeps playing; the **pointer/click no longer takes over**. (Pointer-ignored is an explicit assumption — see Risks; ESC is the only non-movement special case.)
4. **AC4 — Unattended demo lifecycle unchanged.** With no input, a demo run still plays to completion and follows the existing demo lifecycle (auto `GameOverScene` demo dwell → return to the menu, non-scoring). Narrowing the take-over must not affect this path.
5. **AC5 — Normal play unaffected.** Outside demo mode no take-over listener is registered; ESC still toggles pause; keyboard and pointer behaviour are byte-for-byte unchanged.
6. **AC6 — Tests.** Automated tests cover: ESC returns to `MenuScene`; a movement key takes over; a non-movement key does not take over; the pointer does not take over; ESC does not pause while demoing; normal play is unaffected; listeners are cleaned up on take-over, ESC-exit and shutdown.
7. **AC7 — Documentation.** README (attract/demo section), the Game Design Document attract/demo subsection and the affected code comments are updated to describe ESC → main menu and movement-key take-over.
8. **AC8 — Quality gates.** Typecheck and build pass, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Demo-only change.** Only the demo/attract path may change behaviour; normal play must be unchanged (AC5).
- **Gym↔game parity.** Take-over/demo mode is `PlayScene`-only (gyms have no demo mode); no divergence is expected. Confirm no shared-core (`src/scenes/core/`) change is required; if one is, apply it consistently.
- **Single source of movement keys.** Derive the take-over key set from the same source as normal play (`this.cursors` arrow keys + the resolved `moveUp`/`moveDown`/`moveLeft`/`moveRight` bindings produced by `_applyBindings()`), so custom bindings are honoured.
- **ESC/pause arbitration.** The existing ESC → `togglePause()` handler must not also fire while demo mode is on; exactly one ESC action (return to menu) applies in demo.
- **No new dependencies.**

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`
  - `_enableDemoTakeOver()` (~line 2264) registers a broad `this.input.keyboard?.on('keydown', handler)` **and** `this.input.on('pointerdown', handler)`, both calling `this.setDemoMode(false)` in place.
  - `_disableDemoTakeOver()` (~line 2280) removes those listeners; called on take-over, on `setDemoMode(false)`, in `_finishRun` and on shutdown (no cross-session leak).
  - `create()` registers ESC → `this.togglePause()` (~lines 560–565); demo mode does not override it, so today ESC during a demo opens the pause menu.
  - `setDemoMode(demo)` (public) turns demo on/off and enables/disables take-over.
  - Movement keys: `this.cursors = this.input.keyboard.createCursorKeys()` and `this.wasd` built in `_applyBindings()` from the resolved settings bindings.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — `startDemo()` starts `PlayScene` with `{ demo: true }`; the idle-attract timer restarts the demo after 15 s of menu inactivity.
- Docs describing the current "any key or pointer takes over" behaviour: `README.md` (~line 363 and the run instructions ~line 386) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §**Attract / demo mode**, line 159 ("**Take over:** pressing any key or the pointer leaves demo mode in place").

## Desired change

- Replace the broad demo take-over listeners in `PlayScene` with:
  - an **ESC handler active only in demo mode** that returns to `MenuScene` (e.g. `this.scene.start('MenuScene')`) — it must not pause;
  - a **narrow `keydown` handler** that takes over (`setDemoMode(false)`) only when the pressed key is a movement key (arrow key or the configured movement binding);
  - **no `pointerdown` take-over**.
- Suppress / bypass the normal ESC → `togglePause()` path while demo mode is on so only the return-to-menu action runs.
- Keep the existing cleanup semantics (rename `_enableDemoTakeOver`/`_disableDemoTakeOver` only if it improves clarity), so no listener leaks across take-over, run end or shutdown.
- Update the README and GDD attract/demo text, and the affected code comments, to the new behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — **Edit**: narrow movement-key take-over, demo ESC → `MenuScene`, suppress pause-ESC in demo, listener cleanup.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — **Edit**: unit tests for ESC→menu, pause suppression, movement-key take-over, non-movement-key ignored, pointer ignored, cleanup.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` — **Edit**: adjust/extend the existing demo take-over test (currently `ArrowLeft`, a movement key — still valid) and add a non-movement-key no-op case if appropriate.
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — **Edit**: integration coverage that ESC returns to the live `MenuScene`, a movement key takes over, and other input is a no-op.
- `README.md` — **Edit**: attract/demo description (line 363) and the "press any key to take over" run instruction (line 386).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — **Edit**: attract/demo subsection, "Take over" bullet (line 159).

## Risks and assumptions

**Risks**

- **ESC/pause double-fire (medium).** If both the demo ESC handler and the existing pause handler fire, ESC could open the pause menu and/or return to the menu. Mitigation: gate `togglePause()` on `!this.demoMode` (or route ESC through one handler) and assert both outcomes in tests.
- **Key-matching correctness (medium).** Matching a `KeyboardEvent` by `event.key` is layout/rebind sensitive. Mitigation: compare against the same resolved bindings/arrow keys used for movement, and cover rebinds where practical.
- **Test churn (low).** Existing tests assert the broad take-over (e.g. `MenuScene.test.ts` "pressing a control during the demo takes over" uses `ArrowLeft` — a movement key, so it stays valid; check `demoMode.integration.test.ts` for pointer take-over assertions).
- **Choice-overlay edge case (low).** While the hold-full `MineralChoiceScene` overlay is open in a demo run (`PlayScene` paused, overlay launched), keyboard events may still reach `PlayScene`'s listeners. The narrowed handlers must not misfire there; the existing bot auto-select (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`) already unsticks the demo. Verify ESC/movement keys during the overlay do not break the overlay or the run.
- **Attract-loop restart (low).** After ESC → menu, the 15 s idle-attract timer restarts, so the demo restarts if left untouched. This is existing menu behaviour, not a regression.
- **Scope-creep (low).** Re-adding take-over on additional keys, changing the pause model, or altering capture tooling are **out of scope**; record any such opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

**Assumptions (producer-validatable)**

- The **pointer is ignored** in demo mode — the operator listed only ESC plus W/A/S/D/arrow keys, so a stray click should not stop the demo. (One-line change to restore pointer take-over if this is wrong.)
- ESC returns to the menu **immediately**, abandoning the demo run without the game-over dwell or any scoring.
- Disabling pause while demoing is acceptable — pausing an unattended demo is not meaningful, and ESC already means "leave the demo".
- The take-over key set is the **movement keys only** (arrow keys + configured movement bindings), including S / down, since that is what "movement keys" means to the player even though the bot itself never reverses.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUX4966Z0009P9Q** — Attract/demo entry point in MenuScene — *completed*. Introduced the press-to-take-over behaviour (AC3) that this item narrows.
- **AH-0MUX495VG0014MIY** — Demo mode engine: input seam and lifecycle in PlayScene — *completed*. Owns `setDemoMode`/`getBotInput` and the demo lifecycle.
- **AH-0MUXZ4CAE008QRFZ** — Demo-mode game-over dwell — *completed*. The unattended demo return path that AC4 preserves.
- **AH-0MUY4881P007FJ8R** — Bot still controls the player after Watch Demo then Play Game — *completed*. The start-data contract; interaction with ESC→menu must be checked.
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ** — Smart capture bot (parent epic) — *completed*. Parent of the demo-mode work.
- **AH-0MUX4975J0045VDZ** — Documentation for attract/demo mode and bot — *completed*. Prior documentation that AC7 updates.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — What input should take over / exit the demo?** (Options: (a) ignore everything except ESC; (b) ignore non-ESC keys but keep pointer take-over.) Answer (operator): *"ESC but let AWSD or arrow keys allow the player to take control"* — i.e. keep take-over but only on movement keys; ESC is the only exit. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — What should ESC do during the demo, given ESC already toggles the pause menu?** (Options: (a) return directly to the main menu with pause disabled while demoing; (b) ESC opens pause, second ESC returns to menu.) Answer (operator): (a). Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Keep a take-over path at all?** (Options: (a) remove take-over entirely; (b) keep it on an explicit key.) Answer (operator): *"see 1"* — keep take-over, bound to movement keys only. Source: interactive reply.
- **Assumption A1 — pointer behaviour.** The operator's answer to Q1 named only keyboard movement keys, so the pointer is treated as ignored in demo mode. Marked as an assumption to be validated; trivially reversible. Source: inference from Q1 (not separately confirmed).


## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUXZ4BXK001QCEK** – Emit dev-gated end-of-run signal (completed)
- **AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL** – Create Dev Utilities gym scene with curve editor and wave preview (completed)

- `README.md` — matched: attract, back, behaviour, click, context, control, critical, currently, demo, effect, esc, exits, key, keyboard, keys, limit, main, menu, mode, movement, over, place, player, pointer, press, priority, remove, return, returns, right, seed, stops, summary, take, target, when

# Intake Brief — Tests for narrowed demo take-over and ESC to menu

## Problem statement

Tests are required to verify the narrowed demo take-over behaviour: in attract/demo mode, only ESC returns to the main menu and movement keys (W/A/S/D or arrows) take over in place; all other input is ignored. These tests must cover the full test suite as specified by parent AC6 (AH-0MUYJRHMC0038RAS).

## Users

- **As a test engineer**, I want automated tests that verify the narrowed demo take-over behaviour so that regressions are caught.
- **As a producer**, I want measurable test coverage so that the parent AC6 can be verified as complete.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **PlayScene.test.ts — Unit tests (describe block "Demo take-over"):**
   a. ESC in demo mode returns to MenuScene (not pause, not take-over)
   b. A movement key (ArrowLeft, W, A, S, D per bindings) takes over
   c. A non-movement key (Tab, Enter, Space, F5) does NOT take over
   d. A pointer click does NOT take over
   e. ESC in non-demo play still toggles pause (unchanged)
   f. Listeners are cleaned up on take-over, ESC-exit and shutdown
   g. Custom movement bindings are honoured (rebind WASD to different keys)

2. **demoMode.integration.test.ts — Integration tests:**
   a. ESC during demo returns to live MenuScene (not just sets a flag)
   b. Movement key during demo takes over and run continues
   c. Non-movement input during demo is a no-op, demo keeps going
   d. Demo lifecycle (death → dwell → auto-return) still works
   e. Normal play after demo-take-over is unchanged

3. **MenuScene.test.ts — Adjust existing demo test:**
   a. Existing "pressing a control during the demo takes over" uses ArrowLeft (movement key) — still valid
   b. Non-movement input during demo is ignored (demo keeps running)

## Constraints

- All tests must pass.
- Tests should cover both unit and integration scenarios.
- The test suite should not have false positives (passing tests for behaviour that isn't actually implemented).

## Existing state

- **PlayScene.test.ts** — contains a "Narrowed demo take-over (AH-0MUYP6M6W006Z1AY)" describe block with 9 unit tests covering items 1a–1g (except shutdown cleanup not independently tested).

## Goal

As a producer, I want `npm run capture` to record multiple gameplay clips in a single invocation, so that collecting a batch of N clips does not require an external bash loop that re-boots the Vite dev server, re-warms the game and re-installs Playwright bookkeeping on every iteration.

## Context

`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (see `package.json` script `capture`) currently records exactly **one** clip per invocation. The output path defaults to `capture-output/gameplay-<ISO-timestamp>.webm` (ms precision) or an explicit `--output`. There is no `--count`/`-n` flag.

Current workaround is a shell loop:

```bash
for i in {1..50}; do npm run capture || break; done
```

This works but is slow (each run boots its own dev server, warmup, then a full run + tail) and cannot reuse a kept server (`--keep-server`) across iterations cleanly.

## Expected behaviour

- New flag `--count <n>` with alias `-n <n>`, defaulting to `1` (preserving existing behaviour).
- The script performs `n` capture iterations in one process, reusing the dev server and browser resources where practical.
- Each iteration writes its own file; when `--output` is not supplied, continue using the timestamped default naming and guarantee uniqueness across iterations (e.g. include the iteration index / suffix, since same-ms timestamps collide within a tight loop).
- When `--output` **is** supplied with `--count > 1`, either reject the combination with a clear error or infer an indexed suffix (`demo-1.webm`, `demo-2.webm`, ...) — pick one and document it in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the script's usage comment.
- `--scripted`, `--scenario`, `--tail`, `--max-duration`, `--warmup` apply to every iteration.
- `--json` reports one result object per iteration (or an array) with the produced files/probes.
- A failure in one iteration must be attributable: the summary must name the failing iteration, and the exit code must be non-zero (document whether later iterations are skipped or continued).

## Suggested implementation approach

- Extend `parseCaptureArgs` (`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`) with `--count`/`-n`, validated as a positive integer.
- Wrap the existing single-capture flow in an iteration loop that keeps the server/browser alive between iterations where safe (reload rather than relaunch, if the run-end signal allows).
- Extend the output-path resolver to always produce unique names for multi-iteration runs.
- Update `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the script header usage block.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run capture -- --count 3` produces 3 distinct non-trivial `.webm` files in `capture-output/` and exits 0.
- [ ] `-n` is accepted as an alias for `--count`.
- [ ] Omitting `--count` behaves exactly as today (single clip).
- [ ] `--count` with a non-positive / non-numeric value fails fast with a clear message and non-zero exit code.
- [ ] Multi-iteration runs reuse a single dev server (no repeated boot per iteration) — verified by log/probe evidence or a test.
- [ ] `--output` + `--count > 1` behaviour is deterministic, documented and covered by a test.
- [ ] `--json` output reports per-iteration results including file paths.
- [ ] `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents `--count`/`-n` and the output-naming rules.
- [ ] Unit tests cover arg parsing (default, valid, invalid, alias) and the multi-output path resolver.

# CI: Pages deploy `npm ci` fails under npm 10 due to `file:` ToneForge `optionalDependencies` — switch ToneForge to a required dependency

## Problem

The GitHub Pages deploy workflow fails at `npm ci` under npm 10 (Node 20) because `optionalDependencies.toneforge = "file:../ToneForge"` references a sibling checkout that does not exist in CI. npm 10 validates the lockfile before it can skip the optional dependency, causing an `EUSAGE` error.

The proposed fix of removing the dependency entirely was rejected: ToneForge will become a required dependency regardless, so it should be declared as such now.

## Users

- **Release operator** — blocked from shipping v0.1.10 because the Pages build fails on a release tag.
- **CI** — the tag-triggered `deploy-pages.yml` workflow must succeed for every release tag.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `optionalDependencies.toneforge` is removed from `package.json`; `toneforge` is declared in `dependencies` at the `file:../ToneForge` specifier.
2. `package-lock.json` is regenerated to reflect the change (no more `optionalDependencies` block, `node_modules/toneforge` entry present with `file:../ToneForge` resolved).
3. CI workflow (`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`) clones ToneForge at the pinned revision (`5934fb0a`) into `../ToneForge` before `npm ci`.
4. `verifyPinnedDependency()` in `scripts/build-audio.mjs` checks `dependencies.toneforge` (not `optionalDependencies`) against the pin.
5. All unit tests in `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` pass.
6. `npx npm@10.8.2 ci` exits 0 in a clean checkout with no sibling present (the CI clone step provides it).
7. `npm run build-audio:verify` still enforces the pinned ToneForge revision.
8. `npm run build` and the full test suite pass.
9. The Pages deploy `build` job succeeds on a release tag (or a controlled tag/workflow_dispatch run).
10. No regression to bundle hygiene (`npm run check-bundle`).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **ToneForge CLI uses tsx (a devDependency).** `bin/dev-cli.js` registers tsx for on-the-fly TypeScript compilation. The sibling's `node_modules` will include tsx and its transitive deps (TypeScript compiler, etc.), which may bloat the CI install. This is acceptable — the sibling is cloned at the pinned revision and its deps are resolved by `npm ci`.
- **Sibling at wrong revision would break CI.** The clone step must use the pinned revision from `pin.json` (`5934fb0a`), not the sibling's current HEAD. If the sibling diverges, CI will use the pinned version.
- **Browser bundle must not include ToneForge.** `check-bundle-hygiene.mjs` enforces this; moving ToneForge to `dependencies` means it must still be excluded from the Vite entry graph. No change to bundle hygiene logic is expected.
- **Scope opportunity.** The operator noted ToneForge should become a runtime dependency — this requires a separate work item (tracked below).

## Constraints

- ToneForge is **not published to npm** — the sibling checkout must be installed in CI.
- The browser bundle must never include ToneForge (enforced by `check-bundle-hygiene.mjs`).
- The sibling `../ToneForge` resolver chain in `resolveToneForge()` remains unchanged.
- Changes must be made on a branch and tested locally before any push.

## Existing state (before this change)

- ToneForge is declared as an `optionalDependency` with `file:../ToneForge` (commit `3d7f05fe`, AH-0MUTYVA2C000SNPO).
- `pin.json` records revision `5934fb0a0835e8b6ee8297a3a28f51e811b50b0b`.
- The sibling checkout `../ToneForge` exists locally but is not committed.
- CI workflow runs `npm ci` before `Verify audio assets`; no ToneForge clone step.
- `verifyPinnedDependency()` checks `optionalDependencies.toneforge` and `package-lock.json` `node_modules/toneforge`.

## Desired change (after this change)

1. Move ToneForge from `optionalDependencies` to `dependencies` in `package.json`.
2. Clone ToneForge at the pinned revision into `../ToneForge` as a CI workflow step (before `npm ci`).
3. Update `verifyPinnedDependency()` to check the new dependency location.
4. Regenerate `package-lock.json`.
5. Update tests and documentation accordingly.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json` — move `toneforge` from `optionalDependencies` to `dependencies`.
- `package-lock.json` — regenerate.
- `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` — add ToneForge clone step.
- `scripts/build-audio.mjs` — update `verifyPinnedDependency()` to check `dependencies` instead of `optionalDependencies`.
- `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` — update tests for the new verification logic.
- `audio/toneforge/pin.json` — may need doc update.
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — update references to optional→required.

## Related work

- AH-0MUTYVA2C000SNPO: Pin ToneForge and bundle hygiene (added the original `optionalDependencies` declaration)
- AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD: Deterministic WAV build pipeline
- AH-0MUTVQDH2008DEF6: Evaluate switching to runtime generation when ToneForge is Runtime-ready (completed; runtime evaluation done)
- TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0: Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (ToneForge worklog, external prerequisite)
- AH-0MUG2CG4Y000LDYF: Pages deploy trigger regression test
- AH-0MUZ9PCTV0050UMD: Investigate enabling ToneForge for runtime (browser) use (created during intake per operator request)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should ToneForge be installed in CI as a required dependency?" — Answer (operator): **(a)** CI workflow clones ToneForge at the pinned revision into `../ToneForge` before `npm ci`, keeping the `file:../ToneForge` declaration.
- Q2: "Where should ToneForge be declared — `dependencies` or `devDependencies`?" — Answer (operator): **(b)** `dependencies`. Note: investigate whether there is an open work item for runtime ToneForge use; if not, create one.
- Q3: "Should the sibling `../ToneForge` local development workflow remain supported alongside the new mechanism?" — Answer (operator): **(a)** Yes — keep the full resolver chain (`TONEFORGE_CLI` → sibling → PATH).


## Plan (2026-10-08)

**Planning path:** agent auto-complete — **no child work items created**. Rationale: this is a single atomic vertical slice (dependency declaration + lockfile + CI clone step + verification logic/tests + docs). Horizontal splitting (one item per layer) would violate vertical-slice phasing, and every requirement already maps directly to a measurable acceptance criterion above. Per the plan skill's step 1 heuristic (non-epic + measurable ACs + implementation sketch present), planning is complete without decomposition.

### Implementation order (test-first)

1. **Tests first** — update `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` so the pin tests assert `verifyPinnedDependency()` reads `dependencies.toneforge` and fails with a `/dependencies/`-matching error when the declaration is absent. Update the real-repo fixture at the usage test (~line 80) and the failure fixtures (~lines 411, 437).
2. **Verification logic** — change `verifyPinnedDependency()` in `scripts/build-audio.mjs` (doc comment ~line 93; read ~line 110; error message ~line 113) and the signature doc in `scripts/build-audio.d.mts` to read `dependencies.toneforge`.
3. **Dependency declaration** — move `toneforge` from `optionalDependencies` to `dependencies` in `package.json` at the `file:../ToneForge` specifier.
4. **Lockfile** — regenerate `package-lock.json` with npm 10 (`npx npm@10.8.2 install --package-lock-only`) so the root `optionalDependencies` block is gone and `node_modules/toneforge` records `file:../ToneForge`.
5. **CI clone step** — in `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`, add a step *before* `Install dependencies` that clones `https://github.com/TheWizardsCode/ToneForge.git` into `../ToneForge` and checks out the revision recorded in `audio/toneforge/pin.json` (`5934fb0a0835e8b6ee8297a3a28f51e811b50b0b`). Keep the existing game-repo `actions/checkout`.
6. **Docs** — update `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` (and any other optional→required references) to describe ToneForge as a **required** build dependency and to document the sibling-clone prerequisite.

### Verification

- `npx --yes npm@10.8.2 ci` succeeds with the pinned `../ToneForge` sibling present; the CI clone step is what provides it (a required `file:` dep intentionally fails when the sibling is absent).
- `npm run build-audio:verify` still enforces the pinned ToneForge revision.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run check-bundle`, `npm test` all pass.
- Controlled CI run (release tag or `workflow_dispatch`) shows the Pages `build` job green.

### Risks & mitigations

- **Required `file:` dependency fails without the sibling.** `npm ci`/`npm install` now fail for any checkout lacking `../ToneForge` (contributors, other CI). Mitigation: the Pages workflow clones it; document the prerequisite in `README.md`/audio docs.
- **Lockfile toolchain drift.** Regenerating with npm 9 could produce a lock the npm 10 CI rejects. Mitigation: regenerate with `npx npm@10.8.2`.
- **Floating sibling breaks reproducibility.** The clone must check out the exact pinned revision from `pin.json`, not the sibling's default branch.
- **Bundle hygiene regression.** Moving ToneForge to `dependencies` must not pull it into the Vite entry graph; `npm run check-bundle` guards this.

### Open questions

- None. All prior planning questions are answered in the Appendix above (Q1–Q3).

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-08: Agent auto-complete plan. Added implementation order (test-first), verification steps, risks/mitigations and open-questions sections. No child work items created (single atomic vertical slice; see rationale above). Stage advanced to `plan_complete`.

# Screen Action Intensity Tracking and Analysis

**Work item:** Screen action intensity tracking and analysis (AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN)
**Type:** task (research/decision) · **Priority:** high · **Stage:** intake

> **Headline:** AI_Hell has no recorded measure of on-screen action. This work item researches how games have tracked action/excitement intensity, decides on an approach (with a refined weighed scoring model and output schema), and creates the implementation epic — it makes no runtime changes itself.

## Problem statement

AI_Hell has no way to measure, record or reason about how much action is on
screen during a run. Designers cannot see where a run is boring or
unreadably crowded, pacing systems have no signal to react to, and the
existing gameplay-capture pipeline cannot automatically identify exciting
moments for highlight clips. We need a recorded, timestamped measure of
on-screen activity — and a researched decision on how best to compute it.

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a game designer**, I can view a time-series of on-screen action
  intensity for a run, so I can evaluate pacing and identify boring or
  over-crowded segments.
- **As a game designer**, I can feed action-intensity data into future pacing
  / adaptive-difficulty work so the game maintains engaging but readable
  gameplay.
- **As a video editor**, I can use action-intensity timestamps to
  automatically select highlight clips from captured gameplay.
- **As a player**, action tracking does not affect gameplay behaviour or
  frame rate, and is not shipped enabled in production unless opted in.
- **As a maintainer**, the recording reuses the shared telemetry pipeline
  rather than introducing a parallel, drifting instrumentation path.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Research & decision document exists.** A document under `docs/dev/`
   surveys how action/excitement intensity has been tracked in games (past
   and present) and compares **at least three** approaches, with a clear,
   justified recommendation for AI_Hell.
2. **Scoring model defined and refined.** The document defines the object
   categories, a weighed scoring formula (refining the seed weights:
   player/enemy bullets 1, enemies 2, enemy explosions 2, player explosions
   20, asteroids 1, upgrades 1, boss explosions 5, bosses 5), and explains
   each weight's rationale. It states how the score is aggregated, sampled
   and normalised.
3. **Output format specified.** The document defines the recorded artefact:
   its schema (timestamp, score, per-category breakdown, run seed, schema
   version), sample rate, file location/format, and how it joins to captured
   video for highlight selection.
4. **Telemetry integration stated.** The document states how the chosen
   approach integrates with / depends on the telemetry epic
   (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) and its instrumentation child
   (AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH), and confirms the telemetry work item remains at
   least `high` priority.
5. **Implementation epic created.** A follow-up implementation **epic** is
   created as a **sibling** of this item (linked via
   `discovered-from:AH-0MUZCSJXQ004TREN`), so this research item can close
   once the decision is recorded without waiting for implementation. The new
   epic records its own ACs and dependency on the telemetry items.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No gameplay change (this item).** This work item is research + decision +
  epic creation only; it must not change runtime behaviour.
- **Reuse, do not duplicate.** The existing shared core
  (`src/scenes/core/`) and telemetry effort are the canonical integration
  points; a parallel instrumentation path is prohibited by the repo
  gym↔game parity convention.
- **Cheap and bounded.** Any eventual per-tick computation must be
  O(entities) with negligible overhead, and must be a no-op when disabled.
- **Determinism-friendly.** The metric should be a pure function of scene
  state where possible, so it is reproducible from a seeded run.
- **Dev/opt-in gating.** Recording must not enter the shipped production
  bundle unless explicitly enabled (mirroring the capture pipeline's
  `import.meta.env.DEV` pattern).

## Existing state

- No action-intensity or excitement metric exists in `src/`.
- The telemetry epic (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) plans a **versioned, consent-gated,
  pluggable** pipeline recording per-tick state + input + discrete events,
  tagged with run seed and schema version. Its instrumentation child
  AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH defines a compact state vector built from the existing
  `BotSnapshot` builder — the natural place to add an `actionIntensity`
  field.
- Entities are already tracked in the shared core:
  `Player`, `Boss`, `Asteroid`, `CombatEnemyEntity`, `PlayerBullet`,
  `CombatEnemyBullet`, `CombatDrop`, plus player-explosion graphics in
  `CombatCoreScene.playerExplosions` and enemy/boss explosion VFX.
- The gameplay-capture pipeline (`docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`) already
  records full runs to WebM and probes "non-trivial" content via non-black
  pixel fraction, colour variety and inter-frame motion — a coarse,
  video-only proxy for action that this work would replace/augment with a
  game-logic signal.
- A pure dev-scenario resolver (`src/core/devScenario.ts`) and a dev-gated
  run-ended signal (`src/core/runEndedSignal.ts`) already exist as precedents
  for dev-only game→tooling signals.

## Desired change

Produce a decision document that selects an approach, then create the
implementation epic. The document must cover:

- **Prior art / research** (see below).
- **Alternative approaches** compared against weighted object counting.
- **A refined scoring model** with per-weight rationale.
- **The recorded artefact's schema and join semantics** for video editing.
- **Integration with the telemetry pipeline** and gym↔game parity.

## Research: prior art (seed for the decision document)

The following is the intake research summary; the decision document must
verify and expand it with citations.

### Pacing / director systems

- **Left 4 Dead AI Director (Valve, 2008)** — the canonical example. Computes
  a smoothed per-player *stress* / *intensity* from health, damage taken,
  being-attacked state and proximity, then drives horde spawns, item
  placement and adaptive music with a **build-up/release** curve. See
  Booth, *The AI Systems of Left 4 Dead* (2009).
- **Alien: Isolation (2014)**, **Back 4 Blood**, **Deep Rock Galactic** —
  descendants of the director pattern; adapt pressure to observed
  player state rather than a fixed script.
- **Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment (DDA)** — Resident Evil 4, God Hand,
  Mario Kart rubber-band AI: adapt challenge from performance metrics.

### Player-experience / affective modelling

- **Player Experience Modelling (PEM)** — Yannakakis & Hallam (2007/2009)
  model satisfaction/arousal from gameplay metrics and physiological signals
  (GSR, HR, EEG); used for real-time adaptation.
- **Psychophysiology of games** — Ravaja et al. (2006), Mandryk et al.
  (2006): event-locked EDA/ECG/EMG as ground truth for "excitement".
  Accurate but invasive; useful as *calibration* data, not runtime.

### Domain-specific density metrics

- **Bullet-hell / shmup design** — bullet density (bullets on screen, or
  bullets/second) is a standard, quantitative difficulty axis (e.g.
  Touhou/Danmakufu tooling). Directly analogous to the proposed weighted
  object count.
- **Rhythm games** — note density (notes/second) drives the star-rating
  difficulty model (osu!, StepMania).
- **RTS / esports** — Actions Per Minute (APM), supply/unit counts as
  engagement proxies.
- **Adaptive/interactive music** — Wwise/FMOD expose an *Intensity* parameter
  that scales layered music from game state; a mature, shipped precedent for
  a single scalar "action" value driving output.

### Video / highlight detection

- **NVIDIA ShadowPlay Highlights / Medal / Twitch Clips** — mostly use
  game-specific event hooks (kills) and/or audio-loudness and motion spikes.
- **Film/edit research** — action/edit intensity from shot length, motion
  vectors and audio RMS; the capture pipeline's existing probe is a crude
  version of this.

### Physics / rendering proxies

- **Kinetic-energy metrics** — sum of speed²·mass over entities as a motion
  proxy.
- **Screen entropy / edge density** — renderer-side pixel statistics; cheap
  to derive from a recording, not from game logic.

## Alternative approaches (to be compared in the decision document)

1. **Weighted on-screen object count (seed proposal).** Sum of live entity
   counts × per-type weight, sampled per tick, timestamped. Deterministic,
   cheap, reuses the telemetry state vector; weak at capturing *bursty*
   action and *threat*.
2. **Event-window intensity.** Count discrete events (shots fired, hits,
   kills, explosions, pickups) in a sliding window; captures bursts and
   moment-to-moment change, but not steady crowding.
3. **Player-stress model (AI-Director style).** Derive intensity from player
   health, recent damage, incoming-bullet proximity and nearest-enemy
   distance — measures *perceived* pressure, not raw population.
4. **Physics/motion proxy.** Sum of entity speeds (or kinetic energy) +
   projectile count; captures motion but treats harmless drift and
   threatening movement alike.
5. **Rendering/AV proxy.** Pixel entropy / edge density and audio loudness;
   ideal for post-hoc video analysis, unavailable to in-game pacing.
6. **Hybrid layered metric (likely recommendation).** Weighted object count
   (layer 1) + event window (layer 2) combined into a normalised,
   exponentially smoothed `actionIntensity` scalar plus a `burstiness`
   derivative — then persisted as a versioned time series feeding both
   pacing and video-editing consumers.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — **new**; the research + decision document
  this work item delivers.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — reference/cross-link for the scoring model
  and pacing rationale.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `CombatScene.ts` — shared entity
  registries (player bullets, enemy bullets, drops, enemies, explosions) that
  a future counter would read.
- `src/ai/` (world model / `BotSnapshot` builder) — predicted reuse point for
  the per-tick state vector.
- `src/core/runEndedSignal.ts`, `src/core/devScenario.ts` — precedents for a
  dev-gated game→tooling signal.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` — the video
  consumer that would join timestamps to captured WebM.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 — gym↔game parity convention
  any implementation must follow.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4** — Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester
  telemetry (parent epic; telemetry infrastructure this builds on).
- **AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH** — Game telemetry instrumentation: per-tick state
  and events (child; `actionIntensity` field would live here).
- **AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO** — Telemetry framework: versioned schema, pluggable
  sinks, consent flag (child; provides the sink/schema for the time series).
- **AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ** — Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling
  (consumer of the recorded action series).
- **AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4** — Same-seed evaluation harness (consumer for
  pacing/A-B metrics).
- **AH-0MUWMFF3C002WOBK** — Automated gameplay capture spike (video consumer;
  see `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`).
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ** — Smart capture bot (emits the runs action
  intensity would be recorded against).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — duplicate instrumentation (scope creep).** Building a standalone
  counter would drift from the telemetry pipeline; mitigated by making
  telemetry integration AC4 and mandating reuse.
- **Risk — weights are subjective.** The seed weights may not reflect
  perceived excitement; mitigated by making the model **tunable/config-driven**
  and documenting the rationale per weight, with event-window and stress
  signals as cross-checks.
- **Risk — metric ≠ excitement.** Object count is at best a *proxy*; the
  document must state this explicitly and recommend calibration against
  human ratings or physiological data before it drives difficulty.
- **Risk — performance / bundle impact.** Mitigated by O(entities), sampling,
  and dev/opt-in gating.
- **Risk — capture de-sync.** Joining the JSONL series to captured WebM
  timestamps needs a shared clock anchor; record a run-start timestamp/seed.
- **Assumption —** the telemetry epic's per-tick state recording
  (AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH) is the canonical integration point and remains
  `high` priority.
- **Assumption —** the metric is sampled, not stored per rendered frame, to
  bound file size (rate to be decided in the document, e.g. 10 Hz).
- **Scope-creep note:** pacing algorithms, ML excitement prediction and
  auto-editing are **consumers**, not deliverables of this item; captured as
  separate work items below if not already tracked.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: Scope of this work item — research + decision only, or include a
  prototype implementation?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): *"just the research + decision + epic
  creation"*. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-08. → AC1, AC5, and the
  "no gameplay change" constraint.
- **Q2: Should action intensity be built on the telemetry pipeline
  (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) or standalone? Should the telemetry item's priority
  be raised?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): *"part of it, ensure the telemetry
  item is at least high priority"*. Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-08.
  Verified: telemetry epic AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4, framework
  AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO and instrumentation AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH are already
  `high`. → AC4 and the reuse constraint.
- **Q3: Should the research refine the seed scoring weights, or treat them
  as definitive?**
  Answer (operator, interactive reply): *"refining included"*. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-10-08. → AC2.

---

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUII39KX007YUQ0** – Shared player-control step across all scenes (open)
- **AH-0MUIYX1EE008FVS8** – Phase shift needs to be auto-applied when needed (completed)
